4 mi and area 1
2 square-mile?

332D8291CB1B4D1CAEB83FE14BA8B4EF.description:
Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication and division to divide
fractions by fractions.

3B411F6DCD774AB1BB4996F24BF5D9A9.description:
Use ratio reasoning to convert measurement units; manipulate
and transform units appropriately when multiplying or dividing
quantities.

5447FCA0362C4626BC62DC394CFB2CD6.description:
Find a percentage of a quantity as a rate per 100; solve
problems involving finding the whole, given a part and the
percentage. For example, 30% of a quantity means 30
100
times
the quantity.

8794D981854A448383D93E014D428EFB.description:
Use unit rates and scaling to solve problems about
proportional relationships, including problems involving unit
pricing and constant speed.

1D566110902748198149D579F98E1630.description:
Make tables of equivalent ratios relating quantities with wholenumber measurements, find missing values in the tables, and
plot the pairs of values on the coordinate plane. Use tables to
compare ratios.

E66D5DD573A4468EBDFB7AED45DA5935.description:
Use ratio and rate reasoning to solve real-world and
mathematical problems, by reasoning about tables of equivalent ratios,
tape diagrams, double number line diagrams, or equations.

21B36A69A2A142B3BF832F1C6DEDCB35.description:
Understand the concept of a unit rate a/b associated with a
ratio a:b with 𝑏𝑏 ≠ 0, and use rate language in the context of a ratio
relationship. For example, “This recipe has a ratio of 3 cups of flour to
4 cups of sugar, so there is 3
4 cup of flour for each cup of sugar.” “We
paid $75 for 15 hamburgers, which is a rate of $5 per hamburger.”
Expectations for unit rates in this grade are limited to non-complex
fractions.

180A6382E4B44D58871F241953819B55.description:
Understand the concept of a ratio and use ratio language to
describe a ratio relationship between two quantities. For example, “The
ratio of wings to beaks in the bird house at the zoo was 2: 1, because
for every 2 wings there was 1 beak.” “For every vote candidate A
received, candidate C received nearly three votes. ”

07BD99A8D7784D3E90E3E1BDC4224DAD.description: Apply ratio concepts and use ratio reasoning to solve problems.

document.title: Iowa Academic Standards for Mathematics

56F989079F614CD6A3D34A74794CF046.description:
Calculate probabilities of compound events using organized
lists, tables, tree diagrams, and simulation. For example, Calculate the
probability of “rolling double sixes.” Use a simulation to approximate the
answer to the question. For example, if 40% of blood donors have type A
blood, what is the probability that it will take at least 4 blood donors to
find one with type A blood?

6239B379C9A94DFD83875887FD174319.description:
Calculate probabilities of simple events under an assumption of
equal probability for all outcomes. For example, suppose that one
student in seventh grade will be chosen to speak at a school assembly.
On the assumption that every student is equally likely to be chosen,
calculate the probability that the youngest seventh grader will be chosen
and the probability that a member of Homeroom 701 will be chosen.
Calculate the probability of a spinner landing on a certain color, assuming
that all of the colors are equally likely outcomes.

E032AED85231423CBE6E571B90DF2DDB.description:
Approximate the probability of a chance event by collecting
data on the chance process that produces it and observing its long-run
relative frequency. Given the probability of a chance event, predict the
approximate relative frequency that will be observed, and collect data to
assess the agreement between the probability and the observed
frequency. For example, collect data to approximate the probability that a
tossed paper cup will land open-end down. Your friend calculated that
the probability of “rolling double sixes” with a pair of number cubes is 1
6
(which is the wrong answer) collect data to see how well this probability
agrees with the observation frequency.

0BDC9E7BDE4C4AAB9C0BF0A9FBE74721.description:
Describe the probability of a chance event as a number
between 0 and 1 that expresses the likelihood of the event occurring. (for
example, larger numbers indicate greater likelihood. A probability near 0
indicates an unlikely event, a probability around 1
2 indicates an event that
is neither unlikely nor likely, and a probability near 1 indicates a likely
event).

94833D45481540BC96877412B989F768.description:
Use measures of center (for example, mode, median, mean)
and measures of variability (for example, range, interquartile range,
mean absolute deviation) for numerical data from random samples to
draw informal comparative inferences about two populations. For
example, decide whether the words in a chapter of a seventh-grade
science book are generally longer than the words in a chapter of a fourthgrade science book.

40F4B3D721604CC9A7672B9B1872A5D1.description:
Informally assess the degree of visual overlap of two numerical
data distributions with similar variability, measuring the difference
between the centers by expressing it as a multiple of a measure of
variability. For example, the mean height of players on the basketball
team is 10 cm greater than the mean height of players on the soccer
team, about twice the variability (mean absolute deviation) on either
team; on a dot plot, the separation between the two distributions of
heights is noticeable.

8D933D18EFB44EA29F4E7B739991F5FF.description: Draw informal comparative inferences about two populations.

C50E1D33EA2B41BBAF70CEAC629FBF8B.description:
Use data from a random sample to draw inferences about a
population with an unknown characteristic of interest. Generate multiple
samples (or simulated samples) of the same size to gauge the variation
in estimates or predictions. For example, estimate the mean word length
in a book by randomly sampling words from the book; predict the winner
of a school election based on randomly sampled survey data and
observe the variation in predictions across multiple surveys.

10B0DE64A14D43148E27E097A1A2F1F4.description:
Describe how statistics can be used to gain information about a
population by examining a sample of the population, recognizing that
generalizations about a population from a sample are valid only if the
sample is representative of that population. Explain that random
sampling tends to produce representative samples and support valid
inferences.

8E139EBDAA5D448496C9F8CC42948C32.description: Use random sampling to draw inferences about a population.

39B8260986AD4C30BA2D7D9C67F45979.description:
Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving area,
volume and surface area of two- and three-dimensional objects
composed of triangles, quadrilaterals, polygons, cubes, and right prisms.

38F5D264EB7F46C59FF9EC054A21DE45.description:
Use facts about supplementary, complementary, vertical, and
adjacent angles in a multi-step problem to write and solve simple
equations for an unknown angle in a figure.

D0F16561199B481599F1B4DE09C0BA51.description:
Choose the formula needed and use it to solve problems
involving the area and circumference of a circle. For example, a 15.1 in
long wire is bent into the shape of a circle to make a wreath with 2.9 in
left over. To the nearest 0.1 in, what is the diameter of the circle?

549D04DB665C454AB3A1B02FAE53AB99.description:
Solve real-life and mathematical problems involving angle measure, area, surface
area, and volume.

3E10CF3E709E4AB8A3F34C2E1C61E54C.description:
Describe the two-dimensional figures that result from slicing
three-dimensional figures, as in plane sections of right rectangular prisms
and right rectangular pyramids.

4DFEBD41F25A4630B2EDB7A27E0DF907.description:
Draw (freehand, with ruler and protractor, and with technology)
geometric shapes with given conditions. Focus on constructing triangles
from three measures of angles or sides, noticing when the conditions
determine a unique triangle, more than one triangle, or no triangle.

2AB110C5B56348F79B86C0A278B713F7.description:
Solve problems involving scale drawings of geometric figures,
including computing actual lengths and areas from a scale drawing and
reproducing a scale drawing at a different scale.

C8F769E408D3479CB3C2EE487D5468E5.description:
Draw, construct, and describe geometrical figures and describe the relationships
between them.

DAEB84C2D4714FCF97DB1BC133D7603D.description:
Solve word problems leading to inequalities of the form 𝑝𝑝𝑝𝑝 + 𝑞𝑞 >
𝑟𝑟 or 𝑝𝑝𝑝𝑝 + 𝑞𝑞 < 𝑟𝑟, where 𝑝𝑝, 𝑞𝑞, and 𝑟𝑟 are specific rational numbers.
Graph the solution set of the inequality and interpret it in the
context of the problem. For example, as a salesperson, you are
paid $50 per week plus $3 per sale. This week you want your
pay to be at least $100. Write an inequality for the number of
sales you need to make and describe the solutions. 𝑝𝑝𝑝𝑝 + 𝑞𝑞 > �

7A11B7D029AE42DEAB2BBD464916D534.description:
Solve word problems leading to equations of the form 𝑝𝑝𝑝𝑝 + 𝑞𝑞 = 𝑟𝑟
and 𝑝𝑝(𝑥𝑥 + 𝑞𝑞) = 𝑟𝑟, where 𝑝𝑝, 𝑞𝑞, and 𝑟𝑟 are specific rational
numbers. Solve equations of these forms fluently. Compare an
algebraic solution to an arithmetic solution, identifying the
sequence of the operations used in each approach. For example,
the perimeter of a rectangle is 54 cm. Its length is 6 cm. What is
its width?

4FAFACF79C3D444E8BC893E10AF23D98.description:
Use variables to represent quantities in a real-world or
mathematical problem and construct simple equations and inequalities to
solve problems by reasoning about the quantities.

5241B818FDC448F8B487B3E6D086D502.description:
Solve multi-step real-life and mathematical problems posed
with positive and negative rational numbers in any form (whole numbers,
fractions, and decimals), using tools strategically. Apply properties of
operations to calculate with numbers in any form; convert between forms
as appropriate; and assess the reasonableness of answers using mental
computation and estimation strategies. For example, If someone making
$25 an hour gets a 10% raise, that is an additional 1
10 of their salary an
hour, or $2.50, for a new salary of $27.50. If you want to place a towel
bar 9 3
4 inches long in the center of a door that is 27 1
2 inches wide, you
will need to place the bar about 9 inches from each edge; this estimate
can be used as a check on the exact computation.

D0D7CB63535244E2A17B1DDC3DAD0121.description:
Solve real-life and mathematical problems using numerical and algebraic expressions
and equations.

B4D1EBBF1FED42FFBC494A90CE4849D0.description:
Describe how rewriting an expression in different forms in a
problem context can shed light on the problem and how the quantities
in it are related. For example, 𝑎𝑎 + 0.05𝑎𝑎 = 1.05𝑎𝑎 means that "increase
by 5%" is the same as "multiply by 1.05."

01DA1646755C4FB893B117F3878D14C0.description:
Apply properties of operations as strategies to add, subtract,
factor, and expand linear expressions with rational coefficients.

D353ABE9F578437F946855F6613D2F1A.description: Use properties of operations to generate equivalent expressions.

4BEFA8E237D547B6AB2086C2841BA8EA.description:
Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving the
four operations with rational numbers. Computations with rational
numbers extend the rules for manipulating fractions to complex
fractions, a fraction within a fraction.

A601197E5E624799AA753D0EE95821A7.description:
Convert a rational number to a decimal; know that the decimal
form of a rational number terminates in 0s or eventually
repeats.

9C58417D6FDA4DD39F3B6E5F0AADBFB9.description:
Use properties of operations, particularly the distributive
property, leading to generalizations for quotients of integers
(provided that the divisor is not zero). If 𝑝𝑝 and 𝑞𝑞 are integers,
then − �𝑝𝑝
𝑞𝑞
� = (−𝑝𝑝)
𝑞𝑞 = 𝑝𝑝
(−𝑞𝑞)
. Interpret quotients of rational
numbers by describing real-world contexts.

C86E87E0B1E3499F92E2E188F1F7ABB9.description:
Use properties of operations, particularly the distributive
property, leading to generalizations for products such as
(−1)(−1) = 1 for multiplying signed numbers. Interpret
products of rational numbers by describing real-world contexts.

EA3BA2C23DF34F6FABB35B23CD2E97AC.description:
Apply and extend earlier understandings of multiplication and
division and of fractions to multiply and divide rational numbers.

D023F6546A104018AECBE92C3597FC73.description:
Apply properties of operations as strategies to add and
subtract rational numbers.

28E6D2DA79D7430AAD606A8B5DD18874.description:
Use a model to describe subtraction of rational numbers as
adding the additive inverse, 𝑝𝑝 − 𝑞𝑞 = 𝑝𝑝 + (−𝑞𝑞). Show that the
distance between two rational numbers on the number line is
the absolute value of their difference and apply this principle in
real-world contexts.

A994314AA1F54BD3BCC2A452CCB6D309.description:
Use a model to describe 𝑝𝑝 + 𝑞𝑞 as a number located a distance
|𝑞𝑞| from 𝑝𝑝, in the positive or negative direction depending on
whether 𝑞𝑞 is positive or negative. Show that a number and its
opposite have a sum of 0 (are additive inverses). Interpret
sums of rational numbers by describing real-world contexts.

075D15FFE68E4A80A4EC2BE4B175CAC6.description:
Describe situations in which opposite quantities combine to
make 0. For example, a hydrogen atom has 0 charge because
its two constituents are oppositely charged.

926FEDDEEC3C46A8BEF609DB913A7235.description:
Apply and extend previous understandings of addition and
subtraction to add and subtract rational numbers; represent addition
and subtraction on a horizontal or vertical number line diagram.

9EA49975B1F34AE88D51B7FA2511CA49.description:
Apply and extend previous understandings of operations with fractions to add, subtract,
multiply, and divide rational numbers.

7E57730B89AC4E68B1B2A37F100DB9AF.description:
Use proportional relationships to solve multistep ratio and
percent problems. For example: simple interest, tax, markups and
markdowns, gratuities and commissions, fees, percent increase and
decrease, percent error.

2AB2C2BDAEA242579BB5B9C907337401.description:
Explain what a point (𝑥𝑥, 𝑦𝑦) on the graph of a proportional
relationship means in terms of the situation, with special
attention to the points (0,0) and (1, 𝑟𝑟) where 𝑟𝑟 is the unit rate.

D2918F63FBC6434990E633D9F4C62699.description:
Represent proportional relationships by equations. For
example, if total cost t is proportional to the number n of items
bought at a constant price p, the relationship between the total
cost and the number of items can be expressed as 𝑡𝑡 = 𝑝𝑝𝑝𝑝.

C6FEB435118E4C24A279BE7CE348F268.description:
Identify the constant of proportionality (unit rate) in tables,
graphs, equations, diagrams, and verbal descriptions of
proportional relationships.

42F6C3CD14F146EF91D20FE1990B5EA8.description:
Decide whether two quantities are in a proportional
relationship. For example, by testing for equivalent ratios in a
table or graphing on a coordinate plane and observing whether
the graph is a straight line through the origin.

4B0F46A738004AD3ADC9943A2D5C1A37.description:
Recognize and represent proportional relationships between
quantities.

A52919F0265F4BFFAF7EF9B658A41636.description:
Compute unit rates associated with ratios of fractions,
including ratios of lengths, areas and other quantities measured in like
or different units. For example, if a person walks 1
2 mile in each 1
4 hour,
compute the unit rate as the complex fraction
1
2
1
4
miles per hour,
equivalently 2 miles per hour. Give a reason it is a better value to buy a
supply of an item at a cost of $22.50 for ten pounds than at a cost of
$1.50 for 1
2 pound.

A40C3EAD88BA42138F07D8A55E5354F9.description:
Analyze proportional relationships and use them to solve real-world and mathematical
problems.

document.title: Iowa Academic Standards for Mathematics

EED44B149CB64B5E89456A8697C23C39.description:
Construct and interpret a two-way table summarizing data
on two categorical variables collected from the same subjects. Use
relative frequencies calculated for rows or columns to describe
possible association between the two variables. For example, collect
data from students in your class on whether or not they have a
curfew on school nights and whether or not they have assigned
chores at home. Is there evidence that those who have a curfew also
tend to have chores?

AED7A5273A074064ACE8D0A731F24364.description:
Use the equation of a linear model to solve problems in the
context of bivariate measurement data, interpreting the slope and
intercept. For example, in a linear model for a biology experiment,
interpret a slope of 1.5 𝑐𝑐𝑐𝑐
ℎ𝑟𝑟 has meaning that an additional hour of
sunlight each day is associated with an additional 1.5 cm in mature
plant height.

1E88989B7FE5447A97CA0DFF2566D176.description:
For scatter plots that suggest a linear association,
informally fit a straight line, and informally assess the model fit by
judging the closeness of the data points to the line.

8B57D3F954E74C85941EF5443CAF4CDB.description:
Construct and interpret scatter plots for bivariate
measurement data to investigate patterns of association between two
quantities. Describe patterns such as clustering, outliers, positive or
negative association, linear association, and nonlinear association.

EB5E73542B8C42FCA76738C186211084.description: Investigate patterns of association in bivariate data.

8560FC05E9E5479AB61400D1D3728E31.description:
Apply the formulas for the volume of cones, cylinders, and
spheres to solve real-world and mathematical problems.

DBC567FF2CA44112B91AA0F4876C9A0C.description:
Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving volume of cylinders, cones,
and spheres.

77620A2731C3436CACE4199F343646AA.description:
Apply the Pythagorean Theorem to find the distance
between two points in a coordinate system.

DEA360AB22AF4BE19206A10D9ED1C794.description:
Apply the Pythagorean Theorem to determine unknown side
lengths in right triangles in real-world and mathematical problems in
two- and three-dimensions.

910148167F2342239F4F1CEC0717C277.description:
Explain a proof of the Pythagorean Theorem and a proof of
its converse.

D4E049976D2541D9A88D9B74B62104D1.description: Explain and apply the Pythagorean Theorem.

81770D7F5CF04EA0B38AED08B1F89085.description:
Use informal arguments to establish facts about the angle
sum and exterior angle of triangles, about the angles created when
parallel lines are cut by a transversal, and the angle-angle criterion
for similarity of triangles. For example, arrange three copies of the
same triangle so that the sum of the three angles appears to form a
line, and give an argument in terms of transversals why this is so.

13DA480B15594E638DC77E146C6D0A64.description:
Explain that a two-dimensional figure is similar to another if
the second can be obtained from the first by a sequence of rotations,
reflections, translations, and dilations; given two similar two-dimensional figures, describe a sequence that demonstrates the
similarity between them.

8FB314F76A964637B55FA153D259A13F.description:
Describe the effect of dilations, translations, rotations, and
reflections on two-dimensional figures using coordinates.

E9DB55362B1E4EA4AD6C0019F8F6649F.description:
Explain that a two-dimensional figure is congruent to another
if the second can be obtained from the first by a sequence of
rotations, reflections, and translations. Given two congruent figures,
describe a sequence of rigid transformations that proves the
congruence between them.

4DB2F6BFD95A4CAEBC4D3DA548C22AC1.description: Parallel lines are taken to parallel lines.

FBDFBE9EA17A4EB2A3A262A32ABCC1E8.description: Angles are taken to angles of the same measure.

88A7A4D58B1244DC9913FD974369D208.description:
Lines are taken to lines, and line segments to line segments
of the same length.

E525A9BFB05245918B15C46C3F40DA9A.description:
Verify experimentally the properties of rotations, reflections,
and translations:

B73F12ECE0924F35B35BF0E9E4823D3B.description:
Demonstrate congruence and similarity using physical models, patty paper or geometry
software.

7352EE111B51491EADCD369C4680ABEB.description:
Describe qualitatively the functional relationship between two
quantities by analyzing a graph. For example, identify where the
function is increasing or decreasing, and if it is linear or nonlinear.
Sketch a graph that shows the qualitative features of a function that
has been described verbally.

95D08E4E155F41EE846FF48FAB29EA74.description:
Construct a function to model a linear relationship between
two quantities. Determine the rate of change and initial value of the
function from a description of a relationship or from two (𝑥𝑥, 𝑦𝑦) values,
including reading these from a table or from a graph. Interpret the
rate of change and initial value of a linear function in terms of the
situation it models and in terms of its graph or a table of values.

006998A98281402E87A3C52B2F6C3C51.description: Use functions to model relationships between quantities.

71FE22DBEC534A3CB29AAA29D17335C9.description:
Interpret the equation 𝑦𝑦 = 𝑚𝑚𝑚𝑚 + 𝑏𝑏 as defining a function
that assigns to each input value x the output value 𝑚𝑚𝑚𝑚 + 𝑏𝑏; this is a
linear function whose graph is a straight line. Give examples of
functions that are not linear. For example, the function 𝐴𝐴 = 𝑠𝑠2 giving
the area of a square as a function of its side length is not linear
because its graph contains the points (1,1), (2,4) and (3,9), which
are not on a straight line.

CDC4583F1FB54CC6A9252E8E414BF409.description:
Compare properties of two functions each represented in a
different way (algebraically, graphically, numerically in tables, or by
verbal descriptions). For example, given a linear function represented
by a table of values and a linear function represented by an algebraic
expression, determine which function has the greater rate of change.

959B36677C7C49FDBD34DD47A972DD5A.description:
Describe a function as a rule that assigns to each input
exactly one output and the graph of a function is the set of ordered
pairs consisting of an input and the corresponding output. Function
notation is not required in grade 8.

788A9B9BB40D45B2821AB4357881744D.description:
Solve real-world and mathematical problems leading to two
linear equations in two variables. For example, given
coordinates for two pairs of points, determine whether the
line through the first pair of points intersects the line through
the second pair.

8FB9645827F1454389C2F3784082E9B4.description:
Solve systems of two linear equations in two variables
algebraically and estimate solutions by graphing the
equations. Solve simple (by inspection) cases. For example,
3𝑥𝑥 + 2𝑦𝑦 = 5 and 3𝑥𝑥 + 2𝑦𝑦 = 6 have no solution because 3𝑥𝑥 +
2𝑦𝑦 cannot simultaneously be 5 and 6; 𝑥𝑥 − 𝑦𝑦 = 11 and 2𝑥𝑥 +
𝑦𝑦 = 19.

EC79ECD0ADF74EB58448DC10ECD3EBC1.description:
Describe how the solutions to a system of two linear
equations in two variables correspond to points of
intersection of their graphs, because points of intersection
satisfy both equations simultaneously.

A1F5D899F9294A05B1E5506769C30221.description: Analyze and solve pairs of simultaneous linear equations.

DDBA8BBAE4E348569C4E67C18CDDF241.description:
Solve linear equations with rational number coefficients,
including equations whose solutions require expanding
expressions using the distributive property and collecting like
terms.

FE661667F7734A918AEF63D9EDB294E2.description:
Give examples of linear equations in one variable with one
solution, infinitely many solutions, or no solutions. Show
which of these possibilities is the case by successively
transforming the given equation into simpler forms, until an
equivalent equation of the form 𝑥𝑥 = 𝑎𝑎, 𝑎𝑎 = 𝑎𝑎, or 𝑎𝑎 = 𝑏𝑏 results
(where 𝑎𝑎 and 𝑏𝑏 are different numbers).

51A3811A24EC48268D62CF75E6FC1035.description: Solve linear equations in one variable.

21CB962B554249EEB147F4852130266D.description: Analyze and solve linear equations and pairs of simultaneous linear equations.

D8BBB21729CE459A8F87DF9323577AC2.description:
Derive from this principle the equation 𝑦𝑦 = 𝑚𝑚𝑚𝑚 + 𝑏𝑏 for a line
intercepting the vertical axis at 𝑏𝑏.

16AA31837CEA4FF7BF39B7EA441079EB.description:
Derive from this principle the equation 𝑦𝑦 = 𝑚𝑚𝑚𝑚 for a line
through the origin.

679BB4DDA85E431BB4E866C1354473B3.description:
Use similar triangles to explain why the slope m is the same
between any two distinct points on a non-vertical line in the
coordinate plane.

2FDD49E475DA418493E0F892E8296EDA.description:
Graph proportional relationships, interpreting the unit rate
as the slope of the graph. Compare two different proportional
relationships represented in different ways. For example, compare a
distance-time graph to a distance-time equation to determine which
of two moving objects has greater speed.

AF3E9D5579534294B1F12FE130C52AE4.description:
Understand the connections between proportional relationships, lines, and linear
equations.

61907B215F034629837171D9162335F1.description:
Perform operations with numbers expressed in scientific
notation, including problems where both decimal and scientific
notation are used. Use scientific notation and choose units of
convenient size for quantities. For example, use millimeters per year
for seafloor spreading. Interpret scientific notation that has been
generated by technology.

3635D5C8F03E4704AF1596FBF47D5D13.description:
Use numbers expressed in the form of a single digit times
an integer power of 10 to estimate exceptionally large or small
quantities and to express how many times as much one is than
another. For example, estimate the population of the United States as
3 times 10 8 and the population of the world as 7 times 10 9, and
determine that the world population is more than 20 times larger.

686B8EA552504C22A775191DC3EC68EC.description:
Use square root and cube root symbols to represent
solutions to equations of the form x2 = p and x3 = p, where p is a
positive rational number. Students evaluate square roots of small
perfect squares and cube roots of small perfect cubes. Use bases 1
through 5 and 10 for cubes.

811FFBBD76A743838CDEAC63F30BEDCC.description:
Apply the properties of integer exponents to generate
equivalent numerical expressions. For example, 32 × 3−5 = 3−3 = 1
33 = 1
27 .

BDC0AD31B85F4AFF998A3E43A0CA7FA7.description: Work with radicals and integer exponents.

AF48A1E1CD2B4E96A9109032590BA0C7.description:
Use rational approximations of irrational numbers to
compare the size of irrational numbers, locate them approximately on
a number line diagram, and estimate the value of expressions. For
example, estimate the value of √2. By truncating the decimal
expansion of √2, show that √2 is between 1 and 2, then between 1.4
and 1.5, and explain how to continue - on to get better
approximations.

9275975364634C07AF351106D058980D.description:
Classify and explain numbers as rational or irrational. For
rational numbers show that the decimal expansion repeats eventually
and convert a decimal expansion which repeats eventually into a
rational number.

3A84733B08CD4B88B8B2405C91D82690.description:
Work with numbers that are not rational, and approximate them by rational
numbers.

document.title: Iowa Academic Standards for Mathematics

E4DB160DBEA0458B9B7C38FC3C956EB7.description:
Compute (using technology) and interpret the correlation
coefficient of a linear fit. ★

E9FFCEBFD4C24549AEB6AF554FF10BA5.description:
Interpret the slope (rate of change) and the intercept
(constant term) of a linear model in the context of the data. ★

A1E9AB2F221A41E4B8254C8BE509EC6F.description:
Fit a linear function for a scatter plot that suggests a linear
association.

214628128E2847B1982A724C9E258E46.description:
Informally assess the fit of a function by plotting and analyzing
residuals.

62BD6312FA29417CBD20077742A2E375.description:
Fit a function to the data; use functions fitted to data to solve
problems in the context of the data. Use given functions or
choose a function suggested by the context. Emphasize linear,
quadratic, and exponential models.

867D96C7BBD440B4B60204E8A38517D0.description:
Represent data on two quantitative variables on a scatter
plot and describe how the variables are related. ★

87F8E45C0B5B4C5288DD4808EDA76CC2.description:
Summarize categorical data for two categories in two-way
frequency tables. Interpret relative frequencies in the context of the data
(including joint, marginal, and conditional relative frequencies).
Recognize possible associations and trends in the data. ★

B6D0E6B3E2AD4645B6DF263C65A03662.description:
Summarize, represent, and interpret data on two categorical and quantitative
variables.★

A2C80C4524504EEA9ED6EA286D96D718.description:
Interpret differences in shape, center, and spread in the
context of the data sets, accounting for possible effects of extreme data
points (outliers). ★

1139FB4B0ED7425E9D6C27850E67C310.description:
Use statistics appropriate to the shape of the data
distribution to compare center (median, mean) and spread (interquartile
range, standard deviation) of two or more different data sets. ★

5A2E03A2F4764FCF886753FCD2056F65.description:
Represent data with plots on the real number line (dot plots,
histograms, and box plots) in a modeling context. ★

7732F0F8EA04479B8385848616CCEA2F.description:
Summarize, represent, and interpret data on a single count or measurement
variable.★

11E4343F733747F980F67864DF553342.description:
Interpret the parameters in a linear or exponential function
in terms of a context. (A1 and A2)

5F24ED4E6152469A815591B16C69DC5D.description: Interpret expressions for functions in terms of the situation they model.

0FDD27DEE10C43D3B148F4062FCD9919.description:
Use graphs and tables to show that a quantity increasing
exponentially eventually exceeds a quantity increasing linearly,
quadratically, or (more generally) as a polynomial function.

631D5E9613FF406C8E0D5A99953F9D55.description:
Construct linear and exponential functions, including
arithmetic and geometric sequences, given a graph, a description of a
relationship, or two input-output pairs (include reading these from a
table). (A1 and A2)

14DF52B6E8694B99B4E471B220DD46AE.description:
Recognize situations in which a quantity grows or decays by a
constant percent rate per unit interval relative to another.

E8211DACFB3D442F83795DBA588844F5.description:
Recognize situations in which one quantity changes at a constant
rate per unit interval relative to another.

3C5950F15A3046DC90ADE4F7C64DED54.description:
Prove that linear functions grow by equal differences over equal
intervals, and that exponential functions grow by equal factors
over equal intervals.

B7F67E4DD75C4E6F97942803DEC72D31.description:
Distinguish between situations that can be modeled with
linear functions and with exponential functions.

E1869B5C236947D68DB13E7D7D7F4071.description:
Construct and compare linear, quadratic, and exponential models and solve
problems.

B2B0D98BB987437FA28B2BFC67244F8B.description:
Identify the effect on linear and quadratic graphs of
replacing 𝑓𝑓(𝑥𝑥) by 𝑓𝑓(𝑥𝑥) + 𝑘𝑘 , 𝑘𝑘𝑘𝑘(𝑥𝑥), 𝑓𝑓(𝑘𝑘𝑘𝑘), and 𝑓𝑓(𝑥𝑥 + 𝑘𝑘) for specific values
of 𝑘𝑘 (both positive and negative); find the value of 𝑘𝑘 given the graphs.
Experiment with cases and illustrate an explanation of the effects on the
graph using technology. Include recognizing even and odd functions from
their graphs and algebraic expressions for them.

B768F970AAA646C8907D101E6230454D.description: Build new functions from existing functions.

50A3A7017B5C45A492FA28ECE6F0F9D4.description:
Write arithmetic and geometric sequences both recursively
and with an explicit formula, use them to model situations, and translate
between the two forms.
Note: Interpret arithmetic sequences as linear functions and geometric
sequences as exponential functions. ★ (A1 and A2)

1C3EE8AB3C9F4C4DA3563FB7A29F98F4.description:
Write a function that describes a relationship between two
quantities. Determine an explicit expression, a recursive process, or
steps for calculation from a context.

6577ACC58DF34CEF8E09DB36ECFCA96B.description: Build a function that models a relationship between two quantities.

3059A0E6059E497BA7F5BA6B7989458B.description:
Write a function defined by an expression in different but
equivalent forms to reveal and explain different properties of the function.
For example, use the process of factoring and completing the square in a
quadratic function to show zeros, extreme values, and symmetry of the
graph, and interpret these in terms of a context. (A1 and A2)

010F61277C63447483B5858D7EADF826.description: Note: b, c, and d, exist and can be found in A2.

8C1AD1201F8541EABA92D7B2C3462A6C.description:
Graph linear and quadratic functions expressed symbolically and
show key features of the graph by hand in simple cases and
using technology for more complicated cases, including
intercepts, maxima, and minima if they exist. ★ (A1 and A2)

A21FC924BA824622A6964350513A0F1E.description:
Graph functions expressed symbolically and show key
features of the graph by hand in simple cases and using technology for
more complicated cases.

568BE122A3004AE1AB00CF2DDCD6E365.description:
Calculate and interpret the average rate of change of a
nonlinear function (presented symbolically or as a table) over a specified
interval. Estimate the rate of change from a graph. ★ (A1 and A2)

8F4029CB5E9348DA9320D1CAED0EB450.description:
Relate the domain of a function to its graph and, where
applicable, to the quantitative relationship it describes. For example, if the
function h(n) gives the number of person-hours it takes to assemble n
engines in a factory, then the positive integers would be an appropriate
domain for the function.

0D1396043F844968B6E58390C6F0A9E7.description:
For a function that models a relationship between two
quantities, interpret key features of graphs and tables in terms of the
quantities, and sketch graphs showing key features given a verbal
description of the relationship. Key features may include intercepts;
intervals where the function is increasing, decreasing, positive, or
negative; maximum and minimum; and symmetries. ★ (A1 and A2)

0DDA29583C1648A1B8F660A8F76AF57D.description: Interpret functions that arise in applications in terms of the context.

65EE44B0452B4DF49B4BCDB917D1CB3E.description:
Recognize that sequences are functions, sometimes defined
recursively, whose domain is a subset of the integers. For example, the
Fibonacci sequence is defined recursively by 𝑓𝑓(0) = 𝑓𝑓(1) = 1, 𝑓𝑓(𝑛𝑛 + 1) =
𝑓𝑓(𝑛𝑛) + 𝑓𝑓(𝑛𝑛 − 1)for 𝑛𝑛 ≥ 1.

BA190639B2EC471BA0A3C7CE9AEE28BF.description:
Use function notation, evaluate functions for inputs in their
domains, and interpret statements that use function notation in terms of a
context.

AFED0CDF38334BBDA8700FDC5676F21A.description:
Understand that a function from one set (called the domain)
to another set (called the range) assigns to each element of the domain
exactly one element of the range. If 𝑓𝑓 is a function and 𝑥𝑥 is an element of
its domain, then 𝑓𝑓(𝑥𝑥) denotes the output of 𝑓𝑓 corresponding to the input
𝑥𝑥. The graph of 𝑓𝑓 is the graph of the equation 𝑦𝑦 = 𝑓𝑓(𝑥𝑥).

04740917977F48C98940FB5BDE1C7218.description: Understand the concept of a function and use function notation.

D51B488DD373485E91AAC3400E5068C4.description:
Graph and interpret (with the use of technology) the
solutions to a linear inequality in two variables as a half-plane (excluding
the boundary in the case of a strict inequality), and graph the solution set
to a system of linear inequalities in two variables as the intersection of
the corresponding half-planes. (A1 and A2)

114E7FE8FC0346CAB28B976B00ABBA04.description:
Explain why the solution(s) of a system of equations are
the point(s) of intersection(s) on a coordinate plane. Find the solutions
approximately. For example, using technology to graph the functions,
make tables of values, or find successive approximations. Include cases
where 𝑓𝑓(𝑥𝑥) and/or 𝑔𝑔(𝑥𝑥) are quadratic, exponential, rational, absolute
value functions, polynomial, exponential, and logarithmic functions. ★ (A1
and A2)

2A0D35736A234BC1831D0EFDE8488D01.description:
Understand that the graph of an equation in two variables
is the set of all its solutions plotted in the coordinate plane, often forming
a curve (which could be a line). (A1 and A2)

C739B9BECDA84D0E91CA2F4D6446B2B1.description: Represent and solve equations and inequalities graphically.

B8AA82ED92CE407DB310605CCEF5A1F0.description:
Solve a simple system consisting of a linear equation and
a quadratic equation in two variables algebraically and graphically. (A1
and A2)

A3272FADEBC5496B819C7BD81AC8C222.description:
Solve systems of linear equations exactly and
approximately. For example, with graphs, focusing on pairs of linear
equations in two variables.

255E8552346A45A68D2FDF3E12AC03B5.description:
Explain how the strategy of elimination results in finding
solution(s) to a system of equations.

D501E7198F3C40C6A9D1F9EFBE84F6EC.description: Solve quadratic equations with real solutions using any method.

077638079EF74AD49649F04A3EFCA253.description:
Use the method of completing the square to transform any
quadratic equation in x into an equation of the form (𝑥𝑥 − 𝑝𝑝)2 = 𝑞𝑞
that has the same solutions.

2CB6509C19CA4B5B97D9F4FDCC5A1EE7.description: Solve quadratic equations in one variable. (A1 and A2)

E9182FF3B02E45858758C3F287F1BE50.description:
Solve linear equations and inequalities in one variable,
including equations with coefficients represented by letters.

242F29A0D37D4DE19D3C3D4721123328.description: Solve equations and inequalities in one variable.

8EAC180C63D2413887341979F9F350DE.description:
Solve rational and radical equations in one variable and
give examples showing how extraneous solutions may arise. (A1 and A2)

F4F470D528734CB2852616C17E6AD51A.description:
Explain each step-in solving equations as following from
the equality of numbers asserted at the previous step, starting from the
assumption that the original equation has a solution. Construct a viable
argument to justify a solution method. (A1 and A2)

C98E8D7B9FFE4545A662FA2F88670386.description:
Understand solving equations as a process of reasoning and explain the
reasoning.

B542A9A6EB7D42A9AAEB76CB6188E0A4.description:
Represent constraints by equations or inequalities, and by
systems of equations and/or inequalities, and interpret solutions as viable
or nonviable options in a modeling context. For example, represent
inequalities describing nutritional and cost constraints on combinations of
different foods.

68E01681D5E9402BA8473C29C2687EE3.description:
Create equations in two or more variables to represent
relationships between quantities; graph equations on coordinate axes
with labels and scales.

1FA7A0B6BEE944D4B70C6AA41B4CB185.description:
Create equations and inequalities in one variable and use
them to solve problems. Include equations arising from linear and
quadratic functions, and simple rational and exponential functions.

3682D705AE5A406090CE87F5BBA7FE61.description: Create equations that describe numbers or relationships.

EDB14ACA1C2A46C2960A80AEEC2821DE.description:
Use the properties of exponents to transform expressions for
exponential functions. For example, the expression 3𝑥𝑥 can be
rewritten as (1 + 2)𝑥𝑥 to reveal the growth rate is 200%.

08C6442233C140A99C682CCB64272534.description:
Complete the square in a quadratic equation to reveal the
maximum or minimum value of the function it defines.

17BA9EFC6706447F993AC6B9561BE609.description:
Factor a quadratic expression to reveal the zeros of the function
it defines.

36C781CD97CE46D8A3DA8D45E82B99F9.description:
Choose and produce an equivalent form of an expression
or equation to reveal and explain properties of the quantity represented
by the expression. ★ (A1 and A2)

8E58579AFCDB469E83CB9D92C178D1EB.description: Write expressions and equations in equivalent forms to solve problems.

109EAD8F50B94D1A92AA15947111EF5A.description:
Use the structure of an expression to identify ways to
rewrite it. For example, see 𝑥𝑥4 − 𝑦𝑦4 as (𝑥𝑥2)2 − (𝑦𝑦2)2, thus recognizing it
as a difference of squares that can be factored as (𝑥𝑥2− 𝑦𝑦2)(𝑥𝑥2+ 𝑦𝑦2).

04ADE3319F2D4F8FB71C84BB65B900AE.description:
Interpret expressions that represent a quantity in terms
of its context. Interpret parts of an expression, such as terms, factors,
and coefficients.

D2FF05888A1D4C2299A7A9102B57164D.description: Seeing Structure in Expressions and Equations

74C1EAA86B9D4942A0A64349E5B936D0.description:
Choose a level of accuracy appropriate to limitations on
measurement when reporting quantities.

3281C991F76D41F0AF305997CE22D380.description:
Define appropriate quantities for the purpose of descriptive
modeling.

2A3A7C663676419DB79ED3184D9099B0.description:
Use units to understand problems and to guide the solution of
multi-step problems; choose and interpret units consistently in formulas;
choose and interpret the scale and the origin in graphs and data displays.
(A1 and A2)

DD215280D8E04185913F6853777FEF89.description: Reason quantitatively and use units to solve problems.

70CA2445832C4527B7BAE0E5E7B24207.description:
Explain why the sum or product of two rational numbers is
rational; that the sum of a rational number and an irrational number is
irrational; and that the product of a nonzero rational number and an
irrational number is irrational.

CDB4A659B11647B7A77C8B5673DC85CA.description: Use properties of rational and irrational numbers.

document.title: Iowa Academic Standards for Mathematics

D1F29A87FBB441B69DF3246DF77F40CE.description:
Analyze decisions and strategies using probability
concepts. For example, product testing, medical testing, pulling a
hockey goalie at the end of a game. ★

E2AB8223210E4D5BB270409ADFD879C9.description: Use probability to evaluate outcomes of decisions. ★

162DD008B800446E837C708B08B505ED.description:
Apply the Addition Rule, 𝑃𝑃(𝐴𝐴 𝑜𝑜𝑜𝑜 𝐵𝐵) = 𝑃𝑃(𝐴𝐴) + 𝑃𝑃(𝐵𝐵) −
𝑃𝑃(𝐴𝐴 𝑎𝑎𝑎𝑎𝑎𝑎 𝐵𝐵), and interpret the answer in terms of the model. ★

C3D2A00F0ACE4E488005170450A1B420.description:
Find the conditional probability of 𝐴𝐴 given 𝐵𝐵 as the fraction
of 𝐵𝐵′𝑠𝑠 outcomes that also belong to 𝐴𝐴 and interpret the answer in terms
of the model. ★

0984285077C948F39D0BB6A50B21FA78.description:
Use the rules of probability to compute probabilities of compound events in a
uniform probability model. ★

7577013164F744F694D5B5AF085358E6.description:
Recognize and explain the concepts of conditional
probability and independence in everyday language and everyday
situations. For example, compare the chance of having lung cancer if
you are a smoker with the chance of being a smoker if you have lung
cancer. ★

7DE1EE7C382A42508020CF49C594F978.description:
Construct and interpret two-way frequency tables of data
when two categories are associated with each object being classified.
Use the two-way table as a sample space to decide if events are
independent and to approximate conditional probabilities. For example,
collect data from a random sample of students in your school on their
favorite subject among mathematics, science, and English. Estimate the
probability that a randomly selected student from your school will favor
science given that the student is in tenth grade. Do the same for other
subjects and compare the results. ★

D173DC36D51B48D18B92F3B1C3A735CF.description:
Understand the conditional probability of 𝐴𝐴 given 𝐵𝐵 as 𝑃𝑃(𝐴𝐴 𝑎𝑎𝑎𝑎𝑎𝑎 𝐵𝐵)
𝑃𝑃(𝐵𝐵) , and interpret independence of 𝐴𝐴 and 𝐵𝐵 as saying that the
conditional probability of 𝐴𝐴 given 𝐵𝐵 is the same as the probability of 𝐴𝐴,
and the conditional probability of 𝐵𝐵 given 𝐴𝐴 is the same as the
probability of 𝐵𝐵.★

ABBC0855915B4CAFA783666364984A62.description:
Understand that two events 𝐴𝐴 and 𝐵𝐵 are independent if the
probability of 𝐴𝐴 and 𝐵𝐵 occurring together is the product of their
probabilities and use this characterization to determine if they are
independent. ★

CF3ECC66BDCF41048FFDEBDDF4B96A61.description:
Describe events as subsets of a sample space (the set of
outcomes) using characteristics (or categories) of the outcomes, or as
unions, intersections, or complements of other events (“or” “and” “not”).
★

FBB0DE4F38ED4535919D181D665DAFC5.description: Use independence and conditional probability to interpret data.★

73D63E11764A4C5FB45BC45DF705CE98.description: Conditional Probability and the Rules of Probability★

8699B693D4AB406BA1F5A6F35B8FEC72.description:
Apply geometric methods to solve design problems. For
example, designing an object or structure to satisfy physical constraints
or minimize cost; working with typographic grid systems based on ratios.
★

AC468DFDAE77447D8B4B0117C4B42DD6.description:
Apply concepts of density based on area and volume in
modeling situations. For example, persons per square mile, BTUs per
cubic foot. ★

773FB55985524417819552DF965F461F.description:
Use geometric shapes, their measures, and their properties to
describe and explain objects. For example, modeling a tree trunk as a cylinder.
★

435A9880098E40718FC58A06DE24A07A.description: Apply geometric concepts with modeling situations.

AAE6C711E4AC4706B0131102BA0E3DF7.description:
Identify the shapes of two-dimensional cross-sections of
three-dimensional objects, and identify three-dimensional objects
generated by rotations of two-dimensional objects.

6701584F83324674BEBA883E883DD957.description:
Visualize relationships between two-dimensional and three-dimensional
objects.

0733D564BCA14DBFA7EEE01735F3079B.description:
Use volume formulas for cylinders, pyramids, cones, and
spheres to solve problems. ★

3FC22369C25942708DE9FCE88700067E.description:
Give an informal argument for the formulas for the
circumference of a circle, area of a circle, volume of a cylinder, pyramid,
and cone.

FBF99DECA1F44D919F119909559A4FBA.description: Explain volume formulas and use them to solve problems.

314DB2CA65F34923A135F95666BE393B.description:
Use coordinates to compute perimeters of polygons and
areas of triangles and rectangles. For example, use the distance
formula to calculate the distance between the two points. ★

EFCC43E438844383B8EF080D27545E19.description:
Find the point on a directed line segment between two
given points that partitions the segment in a given ratio.

3FE4DABB551E42EBA427746F0A2FC828.description:
Prove the slope criteria for parallel and perpendicular
lines and use them to solve geometric problems. For example, find the
equation of a line parallel or perpendicular to a given line that passes
through a given point.

5D4956909EFF494C8E5CA9B3EAEE0358.description:
Use coordinate geometry to prove simple geometric
theorems. For example, prove or disprove that a figure defined by four
given points in the coordinate plane is a rectangle.

AB47ED3DF6C049CBADD8FEE2AD850246.description: Use coordinates to prove simple geometric theorems algebraically.

9BE7603A3F664DEDAE18B0D2F708E675.description:
Derive the equation of a circle of given center and radius
using the Pythagorean Theorem; complete the square to find the center
and radius of a circle given by an equation.

1C837644368E4E6490BCDA10BCDFC951.description:
Translate between the geometric description and the equation for a conic
section.

77124EAE224B4DD583C36B589EAFABA9.description:
Derive using similarity the fact that the length of the arc
intercepted by an angle is proportional to the radius and define the
radian measure of the angle as the constant of proportionality; derive
the formula for the area of a sector.

B05E57242090438C91EF130B1ACF5F5B.description: Find arc lengths and areas of sectors of circles.

ED1144B581EB4D26871F9C1587583C04.description:
Construct the inscribed and circumscribed circles of a
triangle with technology, and investigate properties of a quadrilateral
inscribed in a circle.

ACD389D64FDA4F8498DBAF8A545A45B0.description:
Identify and describe relationships among inscribed angles,
radii, and chords. Include the relationship between central, inscribed,
and circumscribed angles; inscribed angles on a diameter are right
angles; the radius of a circle is perpendicular to the tangent where the
radius intersects the circle.

7E3E105288BE49B1973A44ED6BF8CC9A.description: Prove that all circles are similar.

61046D23794A493DB83053739D7EE88F.description: Understand and apply theorems about circles.

4CF9E408D6304296A489421A80B40A4F.description:
Use trigonometric ratios and the Pythagorean Theorem to
solve right triangles in applied problems, including special right triangles.
★

03809D4F1EF645A6A1DD7755C1E8E814.description:
Explain and use the relationship between the sine and
cosine of complementary angles.

57B5054EAC654BA6A83E046796327372.description:
Define trigonometric ratios using similar triangle ratios and
the ratios of corresponding side lengths.

58A200AC28CB41AEA9387EFCC5403B62.description: Define trigonometric ratios and solve problems involving right triangles.

FA97D4F96D2D49FAA5F7E73134F6BA73.description:
Use congruence and similarity criteria for triangles to
solve problems and to prove relationships in geometric figures.

AEA2C362A97448588AC6A39F4D74CA3C.description:
Prove theorems about triangles. Theorems include: a line
parallel to one side of a triangle divides the other two proportionally, and
conversely; the Pythagorean Theorem proved using triangle similarity.

2861465D697949C0B197AB95992CF23F.description: Prove and apply theorems involving similarity.

F95C6E4B35B04533804E12CA8C88779E.description:
Use the properties of similarity transformations to
establish the AA criterion for two triangles to be similar.

B8A1F7641CF44883A74E7AF6E16C9674.description:
Given two figures, use the definition of similarity in terms
of similarity transformations to decide if they are similar; explain using
similarity transformations the meaning of similarity for triangles as the
equality of all corresponding pairs of angles and the proportionality of all
corresponding pairs of sides.

35E5ABAB78194FFAB43AD1F9E043D4AE.description:
The dilation of a line segment is longer or shorter in the ratio
given by the scale factor.

2A6B2810CE7E4CA6B90A1DBE70879ED0.description:
A dilation takes a line not passing through the center of the
dilation to a parallel line and leaves a line passing through the
center unchanged.

34B12131C95D41EB97AD29C7815CBEDD.description:
Verify experimentally the properties of dilations given by a
center and a scale factor:

E163958708D54B519E49E4E676D14B22.description: Understand similarity in terms of similarity transformations.

0115E5D37C5E41ED8B10D403DF7225F0.description:
Construct an equilateral triangle, a square, and a regular
hexagon inscribed in a circle.

2E05DFEEAF4F41F4823D7DE74833AF9A.description:
Make formal geometric constructions with a variety of
tools and methods (compass and straightedge, string, reflective devices,
paper folding, dynamic geometric software, etc.). Copying a segment;
copying an angle; bisecting a segment; bisecting an angle; constructing
perpendicular lines, including the perpendicular bisector of a line
segment; and constructing a line parallel to a given line through a point
not on the line.

886A641DD17D448DB77C4DFA3EF36A5C.description:
Prove theorems about parallelograms. Theorems include
opposite sides are congruent, opposite angles are congruent, the
diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other, and conversely,
rectangles are parallelograms with congruent diagonals.

26736E4F4BFC45288B649D4802999FA2.description:
Prove theorems about triangles. Theorems include
measures of interior angles of a triangle sum to 180; base angles of
isosceles triangles are congruent; the segment joining midpoints of two
sides of a triangle is parallel to the third side and half the length; the
medians of a triangle meet at a point.

8112160A596340E78A484F2EE2BFD66B.description:
Prove theorems about lines and angles. Theorems include
vertical angles are congruent; when a transversal crosses parallel lines,
alternate interior angles are congruent and corresponding angles are
congruent; points on a perpendicular bisector of a line segment are
exactly those equidistant from the segment’s endpoints.

4DA3BEB8ADF84EE1906F893BEEB6159A.description:
Explain how the criteria for triangle congruence (ASA,
SAS, and SSS) follow from the definition of congruence in terms of rigid
motions.

60F3D188336C4F0A9EB02322D5A21E22.description:
Use the definition of congruence in terms of rigid motions
to show that two triangles are congruent if and only if corresponding
pairs of sides and corresponding pairs of angles are congruent.

D8B7E15312864E4C96376C6945C13ADA.description:
Use geometric descriptions of rigid motions to transform
figures and to predict the effect of a given rigid motion on a given figure;
given two figures, use the definition of congruence in terms of rigid
motions to decide if they are congruent.

49B828D5F0684DBE9ED4E169ECF31107.description: Understand congruence in terms of rigid motions.

E6216F3F91B54A8C91031870CD74A4E7.description:
Given a geometric figure and a rotation, reflection, or
translation, draw the transformed figure. Specify a sequence of
transformations that will carry a given figure onto another. For example,
using graph paper, tracing paper, or geometry software.

CAEBE56FFE4148B1A96CB573FBA467C5.description:
Develop definitions of rotations, reflections, and
translations in terms of angles, circles, perpendicular lines, parallel lines,
and line segments.

87225D013FD745AFA2B9A5E00ADDFE19.description:
Given a rectangle, parallelogram, trapezoid, or regular
polygon, describe the rotations and reflections that carry it onto itself.

CC271BF7A169471A98D7BD2CE3DD5E34.description:
Represent transformations in the plane using geometry
software; describe transformations as functions that take points in the
plane as inputs and give other points as outputs. Compare
transformations that preserve distance and angle to those that do not.
For example, translation versus horizontal stretch).

ADDD4A4A9F1945EB86DB4C6512777AF5.description:
Know precise definitions of angle, circle, perpendicular line,
parallel line, and line segment, based on the undefined notions of point,
line, distance along a line, and distance around a circular arc.

2B570AC957994943AA078FB626BB5966.description: Experiment with transformations in the plane.

document.title: Iowa Academic Standards for Mathematics

3FEC1B6967E44096B2C552E137F7B9C1.description:
Use data from a randomized experiment to compare two
treatments; use simulations to decide if differences between parameters
are significant. ★

088ACBBAEC1348A88569B626A4365281.description:
Use data from a sample survey to estimate a population
mean or proportion; develop a margin of error using simulation models
for random sampling. ★

15472A38F2554BB19907D179BC93AF58.description:
Recognize the purposes of and differences among sample
surveys, experiments, and observational studies; explain how
randomization relates to each. ★

A1E3C47E24554502BE94DCF9076E2CD4.description:
Make inferences and justify conclusions from sample surveys, experiments, and
observational studies.★

3305A62BA9464C2289132F126D6FD380.description:
Decide if a specified model is consistent with results from a
given data-generating process. For example, using simulation or a model
says a spinning coin falls heads up with probability 0.5. Would a result of
5 tails in a row cause you to question the model? ★

8EBA3341857F4946AF645D635DFCD9B0.description:
Understand statistics as a process for making inferences
about population parameters based on a random sample from that
population. ★

D34C6A224E1C4D2985B2D0F59B39E927.description:
Understand and evaluate random processes underlying statistical
experiments.★

4739D0413B874BFEAAC13B8421D82A79.description:
Use the mean and standard deviation of a data set to fit it to
a normal distribution and to estimate population percentages. Recognize
that there are data sets for which such a procedure is not appropriate.
Use calculators, spreadsheets, and tables to estimate areas under the
normal curve. ★

75B0651B08DD49AD82A94FEC509D55DF.description:
Summarize, represent, and interpret data on a single count or measurement
variable. ★

DCA5B0DA6EF44190B94FBB74810516D2.description:
Choose trigonometric functions to model periodic
phenomena with specified amplitude, frequency, and midline. ★

4129C71FCEBC499BA24F0391CFAB52BE.description: Model periodic phenomena with trigonometric functions.

D9FDDCD8F4ED4A10B6A4AB0C48A4931B.description:
Use the unit circle to explain symmetry (odd and even) and
periodicity of trigonometric functions.

CB6DC7BADF114ADDB9EBA41D898DD5C6.description:
Use special triangles to determine geometrically the values
of sine, cosine for 𝜋𝜋
3
,
𝜋𝜋
4
, and 𝜋𝜋
6
, and use the unit circle to express the
values of sine and cosine for 𝜋𝜋 − 𝑥𝑥, 𝜋𝜋 + 𝑥𝑥, and 2𝜋𝜋 − 𝑥𝑥 in terms of their
values for 𝑥𝑥, where 𝑥𝑥 is any real number.
Note: Does not include tangent.

CE96AF737F444757B3320C7E96ACA175.description:
Explain how the unit circle in the coordinate plane enables
the extension of trigonometric functions to all real numbers, interpreted
as radian measures of angles traversed counterclockwise around the unit
circle.

7F55E10F3C9B448CBCE01515D13725C1.description:
Understand the radian measure of an angle as the length of
the arc on the unit circle subtended by the angle.

DCE4E47443404328A2CF22DFCDDCA660.description: Extend the domain of trigonometric functions using the unit circle.

01219A8604A34D4FAE2D7C73F939CD60.description:
Interpret the parameters in a linear or exponential function
in terms of a context. (A1 and A2)

BEE219AB6C5649F09192F675BCF34990.description: Interpret expressions for functions in terms of the situation they model.

5D6D6B5930AA49868D91A81AFB0C5BB7.description:
For exponential models, express as a logarithm the solution
to 𝑎𝑎, 𝑏𝑏𝑐𝑐𝑐𝑐 = 𝑑𝑑 where 𝑎𝑎, 𝑏𝑏, 𝑐𝑐, and 𝑑𝑑 are numbers and the base 𝑎𝑎 is 2, 10, or
𝑒𝑒, evaluate the logarithm using technology.

08BE2680349340B9999F04F24CDF9CFC.description:
Construct linear and exponential functions, including
arithmetic and geometric sequences, given a graph, a description of a
relationship, or two input-output pairs (include reading these from a
table). (A1 and A2)

0D55A7FE98D04C948B9A790281091B62.description:
Construct and compare linear, quadratic, and exponential models and solve
problems.

52F0F7C84829488990845984442E2BC6.description:
Solve an equation of the form 𝑓𝑓(𝑥𝑥) = 𝑐𝑐 for a simple function 𝑓𝑓
that has an inverse and write an expression for the inverse. For
example,𝑓𝑓(𝑥𝑥) = 2𝑥𝑥3 or,𝑓𝑓(𝑥𝑥) = (𝑥𝑥+1)
(𝑥𝑥−1)
for 𝑥𝑥 ≠ 1.

3586C71B7EDA4180B12229C31B9EDAB6.description:
Identify the effect on linear and quadratic graphs of
replacing 𝑓𝑓(𝑥𝑥) by 𝑓𝑓(𝑥𝑥) + 𝑘𝑘 , 𝑘𝑘𝑘𝑘(𝑥𝑥), 𝑓𝑓(𝑘𝑘𝑘𝑘), and 𝑓𝑓(𝑥𝑥 + 𝑘𝑘) for specific values
of 𝑘𝑘 (both positive and negative); find the value of 𝑘𝑘 given the graphs.
Experiment with cases and illustrate an explanation of the effects on the
graph using technology. Include recognizing even and odd functions from
their graphs and algebraic expressions for them. (A1 and A2)

D8D0E505C9AA4307836AEDF1A3841A1C.description: Build new functions from existing functions.

35DF08EE6A764084BECF7EEDAD8CCB95.description:
Write arithmetic and geometric sequences both recursively
and with an explicit formula, use them to model situations, and translate
between the two forms. ★ (A1 and A2)

868E39DD9F3A4CC2AD9AD4FC2F358FA4.description:
Write a function that describes a relationship between two
quantities. Combine standard function types using arithmetic operations.
For example, build a function that models the temperature of a cooling
body by adding a constant function to a decaying exponential, and relate
these functions to the model. ★

40F719AD6E2345CEA85FF330C5D1CC5F.description: Build a function that models a relationship between two quantities.

83258D8DE9CC454FBD7EE8DFEE86948D.description:
Compare properties of two functions each represented in a
different way (algebraically, graphically, numerically in tables, or by
verbal descriptions). For example, given a graph of one quadratic
function and an algebraic expression for another, say which has the
larger maximum.

615433A5621D4CAE89BBEF03821BB6F7.description:
Write a function defined by an expression in different but
equivalent forms to reveal and explain different properties of the function.
For example, rewrite rational expressions to show the vertical
transformation. (A1 and A2)

D9C331DD293E43ADA35110FD839D7970.description: Note: a exists and can be found in A1.

B6905EDF6DFF43AF841D0593A45625E5.description:
Graph exponential and logarithmic functions, showing intercepts
and end behavior, and trigonometric functions, showing period,
midline, and amplitude.

784DEDC0A8E14D118A13877972978A9E.description:
Graph polynomial functions, identifying zeros when suitable
factorizations are available, and showing end behavior.

25BEB8208AC84AF3B1651D8080ACD01E.description:
Graph square root, cube root, and piecewise-defined functions,
including step functions and absolute value functions.

0C80F49A12E54B199766933EEEDBDB80.description:
Graph functions expressed symbolically and show key
features of the graph by hand in simple cases and using technology for
more complicated cases. ★ (A1 and A2)

2F63FA642B7347F49DD251186100009F.description:
Calculate and interpret the average rate of change of a
nonlinear function (presented symbolically or as a table) over a specified
interval. Estimate the rate of change from a graph. ★ (A1 and A2)

9657D025F9274C678AE30E0C9A609101.description:
Relate the domain of a function to its graph and, where
applicable, to the quantitative relationship it describes. For example, if the
function h(n) gives the number of person-hours it takes to assemble n
engines in a factory, then the positive integers would be an appropriate
domain for the function. ★ (A1 and A2)

C48D241947414FF489906678FD6038C2.description:
For a function that models a relationship between two
quantities, interpret key features of graphs and tables in terms of the
quantities, and sketch graphs showing key features given a verbal
description of the relationship. Key features may include intercepts;
intervals where the function is increasing, decreasing, positive, or
negative; maximum and minimum; and symmetries. ★ (A1 and A2)

9D75C003B90E4533AB2723BD879B7637.description: Interpret functions that arise in applications in terms of the context.

7D0B461190BC47BABE096E2A9EFE5112.description:
Graph and interpret (with the use of technology) the
solutions to a linear inequality in two variables as a half-plane (excluding
the boundary in the case of a strict inequality), and graph the solution set
to a system of linear inequalities in two variables as the intersection of
the corresponding half-planes. (A1 and A2)

FB6ADF55B8E04F1A86A8122BF1E76FE0.description:
Explain why the solution(s) of a system of equations are
the point(s) of intersection(s) on a coordinate plane. Find the solutions
approximately. For example, using technology to graph the functions,
make tables of values, or find successive approximations. Include cases
where 𝑓𝑓(𝑥𝑥) and/or 𝑔𝑔(𝑥𝑥) are quadratic, exponential, rational, absolute
value functions, polynomial, exponential, and logarithmic functions. ★ (A1
and A2)

E6105CCC985646739D4204A00B2C63E2.description:
Understand that the graph of an equation in two variables
is the set of all its solutions plotted in the coordinate plane, often forming
a curve (which could be a line). (A1 and A2)

8A527110D2ED429A993BB8BD72F56531.description: Represent and solve equations and inequalities graphically.

E75F128146CF45648D80A5F2B016CB93.description:
Solve a simple system consisting of a linear equation and
a quadratic equation in two variables algebraically and graphically. (A1
and A2)

5CD74B30BD464E99A6DB88217D636817.description: Solve quadratic equations with real solutions using any method.

D3EDEB95048E4D8FB9FDB9633D1E7683.description:
Use the method of completing the square to transform any
quadratic equation in 𝑥𝑥 into an equation of the form (𝑥𝑥 − 𝑝𝑝)2 = 𝑞𝑞
that has the same solutions.

CBCDDA3073A048158425163EF6790D42.description: Solve quadratic equations in one variable. (A1 and A2)

6011D5FBD4EF4CA7B5C291D4CE98EBAE.description: Solve equations and inequalities in one variable.

0624A24AC3AE4849A6EA6FB0407E3B5B.description:
Solve rational and radical equations in one variable and
give examples showing how extraneous solutions may arise. (A1 and A2)

5B030F48DCB3450796D3CFE7CA1C9B4D.description:
Explain each step in solving an equation as following from
the equality of numbers asserted at the previous step, starting from the
assumption that the original equation has a solution. Construct a viable
argument to justify a solution method. (A1 and A2)

286B2AE528B9454890BD3B7E7E7ADB76.description:
Understand solving equations as a process of reasoning and explain the
reasoning.

4518F9B248724E279AC58AF41DC10F1A.description:
Rearrange formulas to highlight a quantity of interest,
using the same reasoning as in solving equations. For example,
rearrange the formula for the area of a trapezoid, A =(b1 +b2)/2*h for the
length of one of the bases. (A1 and A2)

F63BDEBF34164235BBFAE8D74816242F.description:
Represent constraints by equations or inequalities, and by
systems of equations and/or inequalities, and interpret solutions as viable
or nonviable options in a modeling context. For example, represent
inequalities describing nutritional and cost constraints on combinations of
different foods. (A1 and A2)

9ED8B8FF98284AE2A1E6F508F7D9D288.description:
Create equations in two or more variables to represent
relationships between quantities; graph equations on coordinate axes
with labels and scales. (A1 and A2)

2ABE682D9741480FA6FE5C6D15740740.description:
Create equations and inequalities in one variable and use
them to solve problems. (A1 and A2)

7342D19611044B36B4053ACB3693AA22.description: Create equations that describe numbers or relationships.

write 𝑎𝑎(𝑥𝑥)
𝑏𝑏(𝑥𝑥)

388889C86994477FBC57215C3E3EF321.description:
Identify zeros of polynomials when suitable factorizations
are available and use the zeros to construct a rough graph of the function
defined by the polynomial.

985AF708D19B4A1F9B22AE936EF7DDBF.description:
Know and apply the Remainder Theorem: For a
polynomial p(x) and a number a, the remainder on division by 𝑥𝑥 – 𝑎𝑎 is
𝑝𝑝(𝑎𝑎), so 𝑝𝑝(𝑎𝑎) = 0 if and only if (𝑥𝑥 − 𝑎𝑎) is a factor of 𝑝𝑝(𝑥𝑥).

6329D07DD46745249402FF4CC863E840.description: Understand the relationship between zeros and factors of polynomials.

6B3DAC9DA8BF4550840997C1DE749416.description:
Understand that polynomials form a system analogous to
the integers, namely, they are closed under the operations of addition,
subtraction, and multiplication; add, subtract, and multiply polynomials.

1FDD26F5CC824B98B0A9F874277E9A1A.description: Arithmetic with Polynomials and Rational Expressions

622C55D5F9D140888950722D32EDB8A3.description:
Apply the formula for the sum of a finite geometric series
(when the common ratio is not 1), and use the formula to solve problems.
For example, calculate mortgage payments. ★

45C817A44AFB4656A0831268919EB256.description:
Use the properties of exponents to transform expressions for
exponential functions. For example, the expression 3𝑥𝑥 can be
rewritten as (1 + 2)𝑥𝑥 to reveal the growth rate is 200%. ★

BE240D32072D4BC39457C42B6835356F.description:
Complete the square in a quadratic equation to reveal the
maximum or minimum value of the function it defines.

57255B8F77B74D86A4FA8A234ADDCE95.description:
Factor a quadratic expression to reveal the zeros of the function
it defines.

F783F0370AFA457E83D3BEEFD441D8A9.description:
Choose and produce an equivalent form of an expression
or equation to reveal and explain properties of the quantity represented
by the expression. (A1 and A2)

D1CAD702628B46679481D6DDD0C06F73.description: Write expressions and equations in equivalent forms to solve problems.

C936E472D1E5412E8257720DFF2D0989.description:
Use the structure of an expression to identify ways to
rewrite it. For example, see 𝑥𝑥4 − 𝑦𝑦4 as (𝑥𝑥2)2 – (𝑦𝑦2)2, thus recognizing it
as a difference of squares that can be factored as (𝑥𝑥2 – 𝑦𝑦2)(𝑥𝑥2 + 𝑦𝑦2).

8BED1BB1B40240D9B5FF607E05081038.description:
Interpret expressions that represent a quantity in terms
of its context. For example, interpret 𝑃𝑃(1 + 𝑟𝑟)𝑛𝑛 as the product of 𝑃𝑃 and 𝑎𝑎
factor not depending on 𝑃𝑃. ★

D611C10833B540669475833ABEE0C838.description: Seeing Structure in Expressions and Equations

3A5C377028EC41AA9D5674E64A37C848.description:
Solve quadratic equations with real coefficients that have
complex solutions.

49D9231E95FD4BE4981C13350A57E921.description: Use complex numbers in polynomial identities and equations.

D513516EADD0436CBC6FF41269817D28.description:
Use the relation 𝑖𝑖
2 = −1and the commutative, associative,
and distributive properties to add, subtract, and multiply complex
numbers.

A34A8862B95B482DB23CB3BE6996678B.description:
Know there is a complex number 𝑖𝑖 such that 𝑖𝑖2 = −1, and
every complex number has the form 𝑎𝑎 + 𝑏𝑏𝑏𝑏 with 𝑎𝑎 and 𝑏𝑏 real.

9E678E4108524F3D9A4FB9AF0EC50040.description: Perform arithmetic operations with complex numbers.

121D39C5940A41C3A6580CE5CC0C2A26.description:
Choose a level of accuracy appropriate to limitations on
measurement when reporting quantities.

A9A08BB89F004C568BCBA6D2B5935DC7.description:
Define appropriate quantities for the purpose of descriptive
modeling.

8833D51AFE954625BE21BBC908AE71FC.description:
Use units to understand problems and to guide the solution
of multi-step problems; choose and interpret units consistently in
formulas; choose and interpret the scale and the origin in graphs and
data displays. (A1 and A2)

6D82C311339346BAB1BEE704AFD5526E.description: Reason quantitatively and use units to solve problems.

4BC680E3E25F42D5A74288AC6B70B403.description:
Rewrite expressions involving radicals and rational
exponents using the properties of exponents.

3C293E32BFB647AE969873C9D3E48D64.description:
Explain how the definition of the meaning of rational
exponents follows from extending the properties of integer exponents to
those values, allowing for a notation for radicals in terms of rational
exponents. For example, we define 5
1
3 to be the cube root of 5 because
we want (51
3)3 = 5(
1
3)
3
to hold, so 5(
1
3)
3
must equal 5.

A3629FE7EA1D4B6DAF69FF3B80C0D1CE.description: Extend the properties of exponents to rational exponents.

document.title: Iowa Academic Standards for Mathematics

6BDBE409499C4E69B3D69B823D599A1D.description:
Know and apply the Binomial Theorem for the expansion
of (𝑥𝑥 + 𝑦𝑦)𝑛𝑛 in powers of 𝑥𝑥 and 𝑦𝑦 for a positive integer 𝑛𝑛, where 𝑥𝑥 and 𝑦𝑦
are any numbers, with coefficients determined for example by Pascal’s
Triangle. For example, constructing a distribution for the number made
for a 35% free-throw shooter when given 10 attempts.

4E6C8F4FB04A4726A52384219279CBE5.description: Use polynomial identities to solve problems.

F8BE94232CEC4CA58AA098903A390E59.description: Arithmetic with Polynomials and Rational Expressions

99909FCD16CB45788ADFDD9EB931444C.description:
Analyze decisions and strategies using probability
concepts. For example, product testing, medical testing, pulling a
hockey goalie at the end of a game. ★

E306612CF9AE49B3834FFE2FD829FACF.description:
Use probabilities to make fair decisions. For example,
drawing by lots, using a random number generator. ★

E05A15464E9948CDB6866AE0C015346C.description:
Evaluate and compare strategies based on expected values.
For example, compare a high-deductible versus a lowdeductible automobile insurance policy using various, but
reasonable, chances of having a minor or a major accident.

04E21F625E7B418897657B73133DC19E.description:
Find the expected payoff for a game of chance. For example,
find the expected winnings from a state lottery ticket or a game
at a fast-food restaurant.

B417F9AA6A6D4B00B171E79C76EACAEF.description:
Weigh the possible outcomes of a decision by assigning
probabilities to payoff values and finding expected values. ★

61748AFAE3C44739B6B06F856CA9151D.description: Use probability to evaluate outcomes of decisions.

175DD52BDFC7418A865FDCB1DE21861B.description:
Develop a probability distribution for a random variable
defined for a sample space in which probabilities are assigned
empirically; find the expected value. For example, find a current data
distribution on the number of TV sets per household in the United
States, and calculate the expected number of sets per household. How
many TV sets would you expect to find in 100 randomly selected
households? ★

9118856D9E99459ABE5BE51335830103.description:
Develop a probability distribution for a random variable
defined for a sample space in which theoretical probabilities can be
calculated; find the expected value. For example, find the theoretical
probability distribution for the number of correct answers obtained by
guessing on all five questions of a multiple-choice test where each
question has four choices, and find the expected grade under various
grading schemes. ★

CC471626113E48D48765DE41ED02A321.description:
Calculate the expected value of a random variable;
interpret it as the mean of the probability distribution. ★

3AAD31481B60404DB5C78BEB75773330.description:
Define a random variable for a quantity of interest by
assigning a numerical value to each event in a sample space; graph the
corresponding probability distribution using the same graphical displays
as for data distributions. ★

8E75C0D77F8847C7ADBF8A4CE001DE29.description: Calculate expected values and use them to solve problems.

F8FBCE3F1BA040BAA9405C9D65BEF8E3.description:
Use permutations and combinations to compute
probabilities of compound events and solve problems. ★

6A4EB1519A6747FB81C7C3AC7C0FC567.description:
Apply the general Multiplication Rule in a uniform
probability model, P(A and B) = P(A)P(B)|A) = P(B)P(A|B), and interpret
the answer in terms of the model.★

A0EFAE613B964A15A018346A90FA2A8A.description:
Apply the Addition Rule, P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) – P(A
and B) and interpret the answer in terms of the model. ★

FEAC6C9B7693419D884162D5116EB29E.description:
Find the conditional probability of A given B as the fraction
of B's outcomes that also belong to A and interpret the answer in terms
of the model. ★

B16D127860DB4A2EB6BBB5E3BA41DBD5.description:
Use the rules of probability to compute probabilities of compound events in a uniform
probability model.

2E03D8C274D54CEC9570190A13A6464E.description:
Recognize and explain the concepts of conditional
probability and independence in everyday language and everyday
situations. For example, compare the chance of having lung cancer if
you are a smoker with the chance of being a smoker if you have lung
cancer. ★

8D2051780C2D411B9B1EB9C700EB45F6.description:
Construct and interpret two-way frequency tables of data
when two categories are associated with each object being classified.
Use the two-way table as a sample space to decide if events are
independent and to approximate conditional probabilities. For example,
collect data from a random sample of students in your school on their
favorite subject among mathematics, science, and English. Estimate the
probability that a randomly selected student from your school will favor
science given that the student is in tenth grade. Do the same for other
subjects and compare the results. ★

C58E8BB1FE51497691286DBE2A58B438.description:
Understand the conditional probability of A given B as 𝑃𝑃(𝐴𝐴 𝑎𝑎𝑎𝑎𝑎𝑎 𝐵𝐵)
𝑃𝑃(𝐵𝐵) , and interpret independence of A and B as saying that the
conditional probability of A given B is the same as the probability of A,
and the conditional probability of B given A is the same as the
probability of B.★

E469A90CBB634EF68C831D7E3E5A86DE.description:
Understand that two events A and B are independent if the
probability of A and B occurring together is the product of their
probabilities and use this characterization to determine if they are
independent. ★

309F2AA24DE7434881A124D16F360E7E.description:
Describe events as subsets of a sample space (the set of
outcomes) using characteristics (or categories) of the outcomes, or as
unions, intersections, or complements of other events ("or" "and" "not.”)
★

BF97623F7E7E4176B33F65681896A95B.description: Understand independence and conditional probability and use them to interpret data.★

2EBAC7DABDD847DEACDAA0977D7D4B05.description: Conditional Probability and Rules of Probability ★

2380F5FA5F734981834222E6D3EFDF63.description:
Evaluate reports based on data. ★
For example, a magazine poll reported on the status of American
women. One of the statements in the poll was “It is better for a family if
the father works outside the home and the mother takes care of
children.” 51% of the sampled women agreed with the statement while
57% of the sampled men agreed. A note on the polling method says
that about 1600 men and 1800 women were randomly sampled in the
poll and the margin of error was about two percentage points. What is
the margin of error and how is it interpreted in this context?

B9A20DDE581749F6B049D61DDDC573AC.description:
Use data from a randomized experiment to compare two
treatments; use simulations to decide if differences between parameters
are significant. ★

E8E20111F216474DB26D1BF2E6BA8226.description:
Use data from a sample survey to estimate a population
mean or proportion; develop a margin of error using simulation models
for random sampling. ★

5DA4115C058D464BB588E5690F529ED9.description:
Recognize the purposes of and differences among sample
surveys, experiments, and observational studies; explain how
randomization relates to each. ★

F512E4D3187A4ED8AB2D4D156D03351A.description:
Make inferences and justify conclusions from sample surveys, experiments, and
observational studies.

25DC242338AF4D70927D2AE3C182D0E4.description:
Decide if a specified model is consistent with results from a
given data-generating process. For example, using simulation or a
model says a spinning coin falls heads up with probability 0.5. Would a
result of 5 tails in a row cause you to question the model? ★

76F2A88AFFAC47F49DA819ABC4F10CCD.description:
Understand statistics as a process for making inferences
about population parameters based on a random sample from that
population. ★

F69A6DD259D345EBB61CBC396D8C7E53.description: Understand and evaluate random processes underlying statistical experiments.★

5316CFE634F34988B8223C513586DFB2.description:
Compute (using technology) and interpret the correlation
coefficient of a linear fit. ★

0A47794602B7477A9AF3A77E001FCFBA.description:
Interpret the slope (rate of change) and the intercept
(constant term) of a linear model in the context of the data. ★

association.

residuals.

problems in the context of the data. Use given functions or
choose a function suggested by the context. Emphasize linear,
quadratic, and exponential models.
