Represent data on two quantitative variables on a scatter
plot and describe how the variables are related. ★

6F6A2F2F53964C1CB97B27AFA2092C73.description:
Summarize categorical data for two categories in two-way
frequency tables. Interpret relative frequencies in the context of the data
(including joint, marginal, and conditional relative frequencies).
Recognize possible associations and trends in the data. ★

BE362CD322AB4BC69A13A7CAD79BBD0D.description: Summarize, represent, and interpret data on two categorical and quantitative variables.★

AF074A4FF96A460CB4291378D999A45A.description:
Use the mean and standard deviation of a data set to fit it
to a normal distribution and to estimate population percentages.
Recognize that there are data sets for which such a procedure is not
appropriate. Use calculators, spreadsheets, and tables to estimate
areas under the normal curve. ★

F5DE397A88EA4FEFA4EB07A1A8F16B73.description:
Interpret differences in shape, center, and spread in the
context of the data sets, accounting for possible effects of extreme data
points (outliers). ★

3A151FDF4E9048F28AF4EF2596000B68.description:
Use statistics appropriate to the shape of the data
distribution to compare center (median, mean) and spread (interquartile
range, standard deviation) of two or more different data sets. ★

A0A22E087AB44421BD386E07AD1AC675.description:
Represent data with plots on the real number line (dot
plots, histograms, and box plots). ★

29C54B0B0A5D4DB099FB0E97240ADD4A.description: Summarize, represent, and interpret data on a single count or measurement variable. ★

5A850553D5EA4041BD66238B3E908725.description:
Use words and phrases acquired through conversations, reading and being read to, and responding to
texts.

march, strut, prance) by acting out the meanings.

Identify real-life connections between words and their use (e.g., note places at school that are
colorful).

Demonstrate understanding of frequently occurring verbs and adjectives by relating them to
their opposites (antonyms).

categories represent.

as a clue to the meaning of an unknown word.

Identify new meanings for familiar words and apply them accurately (e.g., knowing duck is a bird
and learning the verb to duck).

1151383E87324AF1B32FBB353A7F3543.description:
Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on
kindergarten reading and content.

reciting poems, nursery rhymes or lines of a play.

detail.

asking and answering questions about key details and requesting clarification if something is not
understood.

turns speaking).

peers and adults in both small and larger groups.

9CB74553EB7246BAADD513C955D760AB.description:

provided sources to answer a question.

4FB92CB8AF72435198DBCC709902B5EF.description:

including in collaboration with peers.

details to strengthen writing as needed.

events, tell about the events in the order in which they occurred, and provide a reaction to what
happened.

Use a combination of drawing, dictating, and writing to compose informative/explanatory texts in which
they name what they are writing about and supply some information about the topic.

reader the topic or the name of the book they are writing about and state an opinion or preference

5B479F5755364578AB2E4B7E9E190494.description: Demonstrate understanding of the organization and basic features of print.

document.title: IOWA ACADEMIC STANDA RDS FOR English Language Arts and Literacy in History/Social Studies, Science, and Technical Subjects

EF3BF3C8CC0D4EA184B333E47362F5C0.description:
Use words and phrases acquired through conversations, reading, and being read to, and responding to
texts, including frequently occurring conjunctions to signal simple relationships (e.g., because).

C4DE355D8DAB4FF2859287749F7306D3.description:
Distinguish shades of meaning among verbs differing in manner (e.g., look, peek, glance, stare,
glare, scowl) and adjectives differing in intensity (e.g., large, gigantic) by defining or choosing
them or by acting out the meanings.

A8823F63BEE14F4985A7745E47C3DD77.description:
Identify real-life connections between words and their use (e.g., note places at home that are
cozy).

B2135F09463042EFABE2B680CFBD6C40.description:
Define words by category and by one or more key attributes (e.g., a duck is a bird that swims; a
tiger is a large cat with stripes).

E3D9BCED47C345BF852AD1C625317E3F.description:
Sort words into categories (e.g., colors, clothing) to gain a sense of the concepts the categories
represent.

F800C97192944BE8AF15EEA4776465FF.description:
With guidance and support from adults, demonstrate understanding of word relationships and nuances
in word meanings.

6F69604834CE40A5A66775F9BD97EEC3.description:
Identify frequently occurring root words (e.g., look) and their inflectional forms (e.g., looks,
looked, looking).

BDF2083DCCBB4886B69167B35F76F0E0.description: Use frequently occurring affixes as a clue to the meaning of a word.

F595BBBE04364D969E57E1667EBA9A8C.description:
Use known individual words to predict the meaning of compound words (e.g., birdhouse,
lighthouse, housefly; bookshelf, notebook, bookmark).

47DCE6F04FB94E6988BFBB5F0859B15D.description: Use sentence-level context as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.

DA1C5DE86BFF432D8BBFA5CDFE036EF1.description:
Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on grade
1 reading and content, choosing flexibly from an array of strategies.

BFDDF16C5DF7483EB0DA725A25EA59B9.description:
Use conventional spelling for words with common spelling patterns and for frequently occurring
irregular words.

F0045919F9AE48A3B5EA1C474E1BF384.description: Use commas in dates and to separate single words in a series.

FB4C18CE00A4430F878CAA71891E4D6F.description: Capitalize dates and names of people.

B8B997EB83C542D28BF9C7072F251FDF.description:
Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling
when writing.

28790CD52EF649068B7E71EB87EB364C.description:
Produce and expand complete simple and compound declarative, interrogative, imperative, and
exclamatory sentences in response to prompts.

1D4F298FBE5B414EB3B114CD0DC80176.description: Use frequently occurring prepositions (e.g., during, beyond, toward).

358D2F1373B2494981B97D83C7449731.description: Use frequently occurring conjunctions (e.g., and, but, or, so, because).

320B8E627E904424886ECDAABB4E9E4C.description:
Use verbs to convey a sense of past, present, and future (e.g., Yesterday I walked home; Today
I walk home; Tomorrow I will walk home).

A57AE3053B9A46D7A4A765B46AB795AE.description:
Use personal, possessive, and indefinite pronouns (e.g., I, me, my; they, them, their; anyone,
everything).

E7F6D7B837A349DA833A1E23177E53AC.description: Use singular and plural nouns with matching verbs in basic sentences (e.g., He hops; We hop).

EBEC20EC8CC348CFA12D879B52246B62.description: Use common, proper, and possessive nouns.

59B2D076FC654AD09A28DAAC28B887AC.description:
Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or
speaking.

831A6EFEA9C146B6BBC5DABCD443ECEB.description:
Speak audibly and in complete sentences when retelling familiar stories or reciting poems, nursery
rhymes or lines of a play. (See grade 1 Language standard 1 for specific expectations.)

F061BEF84FE348638CED384A845FABCE.description:
Add drawings or other visual displays to descriptions when appropriate to clarify ideas, thoughts, and
feelings.

5B3D0C1DE8C04C038AFFFEC17058B731.description: Describe people, places, things, and events with relevant details, expressing ideas and feelings clearly.

297348EC56404AF9995AB55AFD8D9C23.description:
Ask and answer questions about what a speaker says in order to gather additional information or clarify
something that is not understood.

CB05946745944E409FCD12D6EBCDAF12.description:
Ask and answer questions about the main topic and key details in a text read aloud or information
presented orally or through other media.

B775CFF254CF469283E43458D27848EE.description: Ask questions to clear up any confusion about the topics and texts under discussion.

6CFF01E349024200A5FE8815B34EA3F3.description:
Build on others’ talk in conversations by responding to the comments of others through multiple
exchanges.

D161303ABF3F4FB589A8C004691DD2D8.description:
Follow agreed-upon rules for discussions (e.g., listening to others, staying on topic, and taking
turns speaking).

DACE996180BA4EA783342760C01A837D.description:
Participate in collaborative conversations with peers and adults about grade 1 topics and texts in both
small and larger groups.

9F7821AFDEE94733B367D925F8476BF1.description:
With guidance and support from adults, recall information from experiences or gather information from
provided sources to answer a question.

8F7AC724AE5F482788DD5463BAAFB3D7.description:
Participate in shared research and writing projects (e.g., explore a number of “how-to” books on a given
topic and use them to write a sequence of instructions).

730E665BE0EB4D5EA1B47375AF808BBC.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

52CDF2FFEC614390B9B1123D5CA04FF5.description:
With guidance and support from adults, use a variety of digital tools to produce and publish writing,
including in collaboration with peers.

AE38D62F277C4724894DD38D82FB316B.description:
With guidance and support from adults, focus on a topic, respond to questions and suggestions from
peers, and add details to strengthen writing as needed.

AB0ED0AEA4504DA5AD807C71BDA9F8F9.description:
Write narratives in which they recount two or more appropriately sequenced events, include some
details regarding what happened, use temporal words to signal event order, and provide some sense of
closure.

104D0AFCE3B44595874469E7C2EA31A1.description:
Write informative/explanatory texts in which they name a topic, supply some facts about the topic, and
provide some sense of closure.

9E44A6EF555944009C9287DF64DD64BE.description:
Write opinion pieces in which they introduce the topic or name the book they are writing about, state an
opinion, supply a reason for the opinion, and provide some sense of closure.

A2811D93139148909479F9EF801B9A90.description: Produce manuscript writing with accuracy and automaticity.

D588E48BF1EA4C12807EFE2F96453EF3.description:
Form upper and lowercase manuscript letters and numerals correctly with proportion, line
awareness, and spacing (between words and letters).

C557AE2D37E349A181A3B053F5106EB9.description: Print independently and legibly for a variety of tasks and purposes.

1ECB040482EB4B49BF8A7DB4361C6FC6.description:
Read grade-level text orally with accuracy, appropriate rate, and expression on successive
readings.

B9BE3F64242B4D2FA0FA488179C60EAA.description: Use decoding skills to self-correct word recognition, rereading as necessary.

EF1BB9E5FDFF4F9E8A4B0E0F7D2ED9B6.description: Read grade-level text with purpose and understanding.

65EEBA7978654F4A843D6F8FA1EF1D7C.description: Read with sufficient accuracy and fluency to support comprehension.

C1890AD47D904BEC951B9ECB8C79CB32.description:
Read grade-appropriate high frequency words with accuracy and automaticity. (RF.1.3) (DOK
1,2)

BCCA5BC985AC4CD2B10FBDE89742B4DC.description:
With prompting and support, decode and encode words with inflectional suffixes (e.g., -ed, -ing,
-s/es, -er).

65D5C53637664B36BBFAF91ACF4DEAA7.description:
Decode two-syllable words following basic patterns by breaking the words into syllables (may
include closed and open syllables).

E4EEA3DAA211431197301C8FA457E265.description:
Use knowledge that every syllable must have a vowel sound to determine the number of
syllables in a printed word.

95A5FD0289CF4C129CB0D9EE536B9590.description:
Decode and encode regularly spelled one-syllable words with final-e (VCe) patterns. Decode
regularly spelled one-syllable words with common vowel team patterns that represent long
vowel sounds.

6F6044BEDAE74B96A0BFF99273D682B1.description:
Decode and encode regularly spelled one-syllable words with closed syllables and consonant
blends.

7DC45CE417704463AD5C664DED612D62.description: Decode and encode one-syllable words with common consonant digraphs.

F05B80D6A7614ABDA5AB825073B4201B.description:
Know and apply grade-level phonics, which includes word analysis skills to support decoding and
encoding words.

7D0F7EC481034876ADE4C847250FBE18.description:
Segment spoken single-syllable words into their complete sequence of individual phonemes
(sounds).

D41AD03E584540128E37096D54DBE302.description: Isolate and pronounce initial, medial vowel, and final phonemes (sounds) in spoken singlesyllable words.

106CE4F066DD4F57B96D34E78A92E8E4.description:
Orally produce single-syllable words by blending phonemes (sounds), including consonant
blends.

721FEF7B091B4E31BDA7DBDE619C0E2A.description: Distinguish long from short vowel phonemes (sounds) in single-syllable words.

C56E7445126B407A825AF9AB5F83EB6D.description: Demonstrate the ability to identify and manipulate individual sounds in spoken words.

5BE40D306D9E4E3B89E5DC3DA64E10DB.description:
Recognize the distinguishing features of a sentence (e.g., first word, capitalization, ending
punctuation).

803F7EE6F41B46FD8EA173518994E4D2.description: Demonstrate understanding of the organization and basic features of print.

3DA9241C790E4C26B37E1DD32D15537F.description: Reading and Writing Standards: Foundational Skills

3FE18478A3BA4BE38514D9107F3C66D9.description: With prompting and support, read informational texts appropriately complex for grade 1.

C9D512574F124D46890CB9255081B5DE.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

A3D795D362A7471F95FC7A236AAFEB8E.description:
Identify basic similarities in and differences between two texts on the same topic (e.g., in illustrations,
descriptions, or procedures).

43BB5FA1CA09410CBF6C3A6BFFFF8585.description: Identify the reasons an author gives to support points in a text.

C6A9E680018D4698A18D43F9FB6676EF.description: Use the illustrations and details in a text to describe its key ideas.

6A2187B9DE7A4B1FA0D2E9D0882A2CE3.description:
Distinguish between information provided by pictures or other illustrations and information provided by
the words in a text.

D5087FA924FA4F11934DD362C088C8A5.description:
Know and use various text features (e.g., headings, tables of contents, glossaries, electronic menus,
icons) to locate key facts or information in a text.

8A8BA5A996144880AEB3E01ADB26AEE4.description: Ask and answer questions to help determine or clarify the meaning of words and phrases in a text.

BA5E881A7F7E43EB8EFF56493D95EF35.description: Describe the connection between two individuals, events, ideas, or pieces of information in a text.

F06578E79204452C894760E3C835C9E6.description: Identify the main topic and retell key details of a text.

A488EC7091794A6187BB855C8C970511.description: Ask and answer questions about key details in a text.

16B74A6B710149908855F67A1BC64EBF.description: With prompting and support, read stories and poetry of appropriate complexity for grade 1.

F8CF8A3FD1FB4606B27B3BE8AE1293BB.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

72F781DEFB984CE88A7350E967215315.description: Compare and contrast the adventures and experiences of characters in stories.

E33F86479533447A89016739D94C9CED.description: Use illustrations and details in a story to describe its characters, setting, or events.

A63D1ECB32FC474AB41669EE4F7D9D1D.description: Identify who is telling the story at various points in a text.

6B1108CA3181462791EAC5370DA126D8.description:
Explain major differences between books that tell stories and books that give information, drawing on a
wide reading of a range of text types.

18578DF6CE344FCFBBC178E8C2A52FC6.description: Identify words and phrases in stories or poems that suggest feelings or appeal to the senses.

AE871BFE14A94C3983AE8A95809D80A5.description: Describe characters, settings, and major events in a story, using key details.

8782640377A441358C8AB4B1BA06A3D3.description: Retell stories, including key details, and demonstrate understanding of their central message or lesson.

26523DE155FD42FD9FBD6DD4A867A481.description: Ask and answer questions about key details in a text.

standardSets.title: English Language Arts: Grade 2

document.title: Iowa Academic Standards for English Language Arts and Literacy in History/Social Studies, Science, and Technical Subjects

9921750B4A6C4E3396F41525D8094E38.description:
Use words and phrases acquired through conversations, reading and being read to, and responding to
texts, including using adjectives and adverbs to describe (e.g., When other kids are happy that makes
me happy).

322433079B254059AE4C88257F3FB11A.description:
Distinguish shades of meaning among closely related verbs (e.g., toss, throw, hurl) and closely
related adjectives (e.g., thin, slender, skinny, scrawny).

7F1E29205B694734A7D366DB2FAC71FB.description:
Identify real-life connections between words and their use (e.g., describe foods that are spicy or
juicy).

D64FAB20425343439A574122B5B9DED0.description: Demonstrate understanding of word relationships and nuances in word meanings.

409E9B6FD93741599C6863761476F782.description:
Use reference materials (e.g., glossaries and beginning dictionaries) to determine or clarify the
meaning of words and phrases.

D1568E0A599B4A33A0DD8705A42DA91E.description:
Use a known root word to identify the meaning of an unknown word with the same root (e.g.,
addition, additional).

B7292EDF75EC4FF2AC19ECCEC5FEDA1B.description:
Determine the meaning of the new word formed when a known prefix is added to a known word
(e.g., happy/unhappy, tell/retell).

A56F8CEE7F124B6F9FAFAD5ED80B236F.description: Use sentence-level context as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.

BADD24E2D40D4417A6D5156EC1ACE981.description:
Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on grade
2 reading and content, choosing flexibly from an array of strategies.

17E77C1085C64635B004249F9A35FB19.description: Compare formal and informal uses of English.

BA8DB36091D6473AA1895C46DB479C16.description: Use knowledge of language and its conventions when writing, speaking, reading, or listening.

636AE5A2CF064166A07F34E265DF1C00.description:
Consult reference materials (e.g., beginning dictionaries) as needed, to check and correct
spellings.

70FD09469D95421BBFEE43D3833DC1EA.description: Generalize learned spelling patterns when writing words (e.g., cage → badge; boy → boil).

A64A8B6A171E4D38868193607D710E1D.description: Use an apostrophe to form contractions and frequently occurring possessives.

D9FF1C3F4D2E42EF83AF7D9B3A1F87C7.description: Use commas in greetings and closings of letters.

6D5C01DE95B0496A872FCF9A63D9E46D.description: Capitalize holidays, product names, and geographic names.

A18F631D973642829419796F679DE895.description:
Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling
when writing.

D283A7D7977A42D69A68E959FB65422E.description:
Produce, expand, and rearrange complete simple and compound sentences (e.g., The boy
watched the movie; The little boy watched the movie; The action movie was watched by the little
boy).

30C5C8905EE5455EA7A268FD3ED73394.description: Form and use the past tense of frequently occurring irregular verbs (e.g., sat, hid, told).

C3A780D88587487D8FF17AD30C925357.description: Form and use frequently occurring irregular plural nouns (e.g., feet, children, teeth, mice, fish).

EB01A0292C2A441B8EC2EA9A0C9ECFA1.description:
Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or
speaking.

15441DAADF114BA1840E172060DB897D.description:
Speak audibly and in complete sentences when appropriate to task and situation in order to provide
requested detail or clarification when retelling familiar stories or reciting poems, nursery rhymes or lines
of a play. (See grade 2 Language standards 1 and 3 for specific expectations.)

0A70A1FB793846E8A77CCA25456FEA64.description:
Create audio recordings of stories or poems; add drawings or other visual displays to stories or
recounts of experiences when appropriate to clarify ideas, thoughts, and feelings.

216BA721D9C744DEA913CF3226B1C939.description:
Recount an experience or tell a story with appropriate facts and relevant, descriptive details, speaking
clearly in complete sentences.

6CB73CC3442347A9BD54CDA7C2C626EE.description:
Ask and answer questions about what a speaker says in order to clarify comprehension, gather
additional information, or deepen understanding of a topic or issue.

4A3C19B707734A46B45352D934080CE4.description:
Describe the main topic and recount key details from a text read aloud, information presented orally, or
other media.

D2B74A6012FF40F686A1B96084F9C271.description:
Ask for clarification and further explanation as needed about the topics and texts under
discussion.

1742D13F3B9D4DE0BF106D91D5304E87.description: Build on others’ talk in conversations by linking their comments to the remarks of others.

E991388B06924310BFED343FB5086CF5.description:
Follow agreed-upon rules for discussions (e.g., gaining the floor in respectful ways, listening to
others, staying on topic, and taking turns speaking).

04A9F5F33A6F4BBB9C5BB39C9BC5599A.description:
Participate in collaborative conversations with peers and adults about grade 2 topics and texts in both
small and larger groups.

A59D123DA6164F9D8FA53A9C2E40F476.description: Recall information from experiences or gather information from provided sources to answer a question.

5B0566115289400090898F0A0CA32675.description:
Participate in shared research and writing projects (e.g., read a number of books on a single topic to
produce a report; record science observations).

3A0319C904FF44CAA101E03C6C6BAA89.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

B6496CEF92A94BE1B206D00D6C239884.description:
With guidance and support from adults and collaboration with peers, use a variety of digital tools to
produce and publish writing.

FB6740CC51924F3885EBE86A92164EB6.description:
With guidance and support from adults and peers, focus on a topic and strengthen writing as needed by
revising and editing.

39826441FE524561B0E3C305EC4D67EF.description:
Write narratives in which they recount a well-elaborated event or short sequence of events, include
details to describe actions, thoughts, and feelings, use temporal words to signal event order, and
provide a sense of closure.

861D1CA29007410994B77E54EE282305.description:
Write informative/explanatory texts in which they introduce a topic, use facts and definitions to develop
points, and provide a concluding statement or section.

65B153E44241461BB84CA88FE498A49D.description:
Write opinion pieces in which they introduce the topic or book they are writing about, state an opinion,
supply reasons that support the opinion, use linking words (e.g., because, and, also) to connect opinion
and reasons, and provide a concluding statement or section.

C70F8489211F4E8794C307689884B4E0.description: Produce manuscript writing with accuracy and automaticity.

FCCBC7E2E4A64A1BACD566631CD029FE.description: Print independently and legibly for a variety of tasks and purposes.

CB9E2252BB504698B6AF104204B4C65F.description:
Read grade-level text orally with accuracy, appropriate rate, and expression on successive
readings.

0F496C62B7CC4CB98FC6CB4F84786E2C.description: Use decoding skills to self-correct word recognition, rereading as necessary.

31ACBD04B2444D59AE7E0C6EB71F5F3B.description: Read grade-level text with purpose and understanding.

A758FFE1E746408BA2C012013472E91B.description: Read with sufficient accuracy and fluency to support comprehension

6B2A689930214CF6BEA83A31B3131B46.description: Read grade-appropriate high frequency words with accuracy and automaticity.

AD0ADAADB14748448B6C3BD017ED2C37.description: With prompting and support, decode and encode words with inconsistent but common spelling-sound correspondences.

54B00737F397442F9F7A9CC936C6E17C.description: Decode and encode words with common prefixes and suffixes.

30DC0CEAA87C469CBAE2CCA3AAD4ABE4.description: Decode and encode regularly spelled two-syllable or multisyllabic words.

99DAF748BF094E579662BA2E5E43753D.description:
Decode and encode common vowel teams. With prompting and support, decode and encode
additional vowel teams.

CECD06DC9A5F469A9BC96375365367F4.description: Decode and encode long and short vowels in regularly-spelled one-syllable words.

1D693004ECE842EF819C6C1F1C9EAD77.description: Know and apply grade-level phonics and word analysis skills to support decoding and encoding words.

0754D2B6F0E44A05827E382EC1E3F1C4.description: Reading and Writing Standards: Foundational Skills

021B1A58119E4F49A8CC8085A164650A.description:
By the end of the year, read and comprehend informational texts, including history/social studies,
science, and technical texts, in the grades 2–3 text complexity band proficiently, with scaffolding as
needed at the high end of the range.

5250E93CE0014F278FDFE8606800C99E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

15A88F09455A4C688EAEC6062B94128D.description: Compare and contrast the most important points presented by two texts on the same topic.

FA23980CA4424586A9977B0A7B970261.description: Describe how reasons support specific points the author makes in a text.

0BD420C4802F4F16B68CEDA4C44DD098.description:
Explain how specific images (e.g., a diagram showing how a machine works) and details contribute to
and clarify a text.

1F37E845F68847728B223F7F0BF8D1EE.description: Identify the main purpose of a text, including the author’s point of view and/or perspective.

0FBC31C038A14264BA9CB840FDDFB918.description:
Know and use various text features (e.g., captions, bold print, subheadings, glossaries, indexes,
electronic menus, icons) to locate key facts or information in a text efficiently.

A4434D97AD5A4E1DB4525B01303BF7A9.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases in a text relevant to a grade 2 topic or subject area.

B86CE29B48AF44609714506CEC2141C4.description:
Describe the relationship between a series of historical events, scientific ideas or concepts, or steps in
technical procedures in a text.

EE8D6B408BD747C482FB4AD1EFE2074E.description:
Identify the main topic of a multi-paragraph text as well as the focus of specific paragraphs within the
text.

378C12B26DBF4864A13F4112D7885DAF.description:
Ask and answer such questions as who, what, where, when, why, and how to demonstrate
understanding of key details in a text.

AAFAB33BDBB04BC5BEA1A23E79B89A42.description:
By the end of the year, read and comprehend literature, including stories and poetry, in the grades 2-3
text complexity band proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range.

E19D3C45D5D34E48AA626F3F08A3D94F.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

45EF1707D2F1406B8B025896C18FDFE8.description:
Compare and contrast two or more versions of the same story by different authors or from different
cultures.

DE91B967D42B4E78806C56CB140A880B.description:
Use information gained from the illustrations and words in a story to demonstrate understanding of its
characters, setting, or plot.

E6B2D9A263D74139BEB683130B8EBF77.description:
Acknowledge differences in the points of view (perspective) of characters, including by speaking in a
different voice for each character when reading dialogue aloud.

39771371ED7144AA9C6156ED94BA6F7F.description:
Describe the overall structure of a story, including describing how the beginning introduces the story,
how the middle progresses the plot, and how the ending concludes the action.

E6A0F791830343C1B20AFD67545AA51F.description:
Describe how words and phrases (e.g., regular beats, alliteration, rhymes, repeated lines) supply
rhythm and meaning in a story, poem, or song.

297AF74433004437BE4F66CB2D269108.description: Describe how characters in a story respond to major events and challenges, drawing on key details.

5D661683FD7E4864AE90FFF8CE7FDCBA.description:
Recount and determine the central message, lesson or moral of stories, including but not limited to
fables and folktales from diverse cultures.

084F18A3122A4987965AF1FCB2915F5E.description:
Ask and answer such questions as who, what, where, when, why, and how to demonstrate
understanding of key details using evidence from the text.

standardSets.title: English Language Arts: Grade 3
standardSets.subject: English Language Arts and Literacy in History/Social Studies, Science, and Technical Subjects (2024-)

document.title: Iowa Academic Standards for English Language Arts and Literacy in History/Social Studies, Science, and Technical Subjects

F5D9F9FB1D5C42E4AF1BFD07E39CA810.description:
Acquire and use accurately grade-appropriate conversational, general academic, and domain-specific
words and phrases, including those that signal spatial and temporal relationships (e.g., After dinner that
night, we went looking for them).

FB3D87F19B2643EEB4FAA8A8D3DFF560.description:
Distinguish shades of meaning among related words that describe states of mind or degrees of
certainty (e.g., knew, believed, suspected, heard, wondered).

E19EEE68B48C457BB18C8B6443005DB8.description:
Identify real-life connections between words and their use (e.g., describe people who are
friendly or helpful).

5E2B49ACBC9D4E548ED54B4C2C8976C1.description: Distinguish the literal and nonliteral meanings of words and phrases in context (e.g., take steps).

3A203023C78F47EE897D367F079CEA4A.description: Demonstrate understanding of word relationships and nuances in word meanings.

4F42BBFC7AB84D48A6AF895A44C5D10D.description:
Use reference materials (e.g., glossaries or beginning dictionaries) to determine or clarify the
precise meaning of key words and phrases.

2FD72D7A72B84C5CB3D48D5724A5BDB6.description:
Use a known root word as a clue to the meaning of an unknown word with the same root (e.g.,
company, companion).

8A4564CC1E9141E1BE95EBB938705EE1.description:
Determine the meaning of the new word formed when a known affix is added to a known word
(e.g., agreeable/disagreeable, comfortable/uncomfortable, care/careless, heat/preheat).

201A7AB098804087880C60AB8D6A3A36.description: Use sentence-level context as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.

C61315123B374619AD41B066FCCF8A3F.description:
Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on grade
3 reading and content, choosing flexibly from a range of strategies.

6907A4251FCE4CC098803F5A31B9F59B.description:
Recognize and observe differences between the conventions of spoken and written standard
English.

AB419654D9DA49FAAACD1219527AFB4E.description: Choose words and phrases for effect.

2BE45B67373443FD8362B1C47113A42E.description: Use knowledge of language and its conventions when writing, speaking, reading, or listening.

2FDAF515D67844F29134F272FE49709F.description:
Consult reference materials (e.g., beginning dictionaries) as needed to check and correct
spellings.

C9EA9B391CFD43098189B58A992EC927.description:
Use spelling patterns and generalizations (e.g., word families, position-based spellings, syllable
patterns, ending rules, meaningful word parts) in writing words.

7B54479C425E4B558CC8B248112F6CC5.description:
Use conventional spelling for high-frequency and other studied words and for adding suffixes to
base words (e.g., sitting, smiled, cries, happiness).

C1575A3EA2B445DEBE46902692B9F4B9.description: Use commas and quotation marks in dialogue.

162EA7703F5E46AB92C20D858C4E62A3.description:
Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling
when writing.

F6587866E6B8403EA4BF6969FCCCDB63.description: Produce simple, compound, and complex sentences.

76141453578246F89D8BEB28F4C3E554.description:
Form and use comparative and superlative adjectives and adverbs, and choose between them
depending on what is to be modified.

FE36A965E63F4445BFDEDF75683F4215.description: Form and use the simple (e.g., I walked; I walk; I will walk) verb tenses.

4878C0B058004B63B4E575881240E090.description: Form and use regular and irregular verbs.

C09C0F1610084C9A94000395665BEAF0.description: Form and use regular and irregular plural nouns.

B95AE49BD798410BBB26100BDD7203E5.description:
Explain the function of nouns, pronouns, verbs, adjectives, and adverbs in general and their
functions in particular sentences.

85D517F4EF3A41ADA67012D171839866.description:
Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or
speaking.

BA7263F4B24B4C05B1D8264F627C69C4.description:
Speak audibly and in complete sentences when appropriate to task and situation, such as when
performing dramatic readings or presentations, in order to provide requested detail or clarification. (See
grade 3 Language standards 1 and 3 for specific expectations.)

C51D1BF232754EA3882C4E713CFEE5FA.description:
Create engaging audio recordings of stories or poems that demonstrate fluid reading at an
understandable pace; add visual displays when appropriate to emphasize or enhance certain facts or
details.

9678346DED29419B86443492C072B7F6.description:
Report on a topic or text, tell a story, or recount an experience with appropriate facts and relevant,
descriptive details, speaking clearly at an understandable pace.

2F0C899C1EEF4DDCBDB5D9D1A8CBF271.description:
Ask and answer questions about information from a speaker, offering appropriate elaboration and
detail.

0B8B2D319FF84CC186A25D13266D94C4.description:
Determine the main ideas and supporting details of a text read aloud or information presented in
diverse media and formats, including visually, quantitatively, and orally.

94E5F90382AD42AF8198A7F5CCBCF307.description: Explain their own ideas and understanding in light of the discussion.

22E05A2459C646CAAEAF647BF67BC882.description:
Ask relevant and clarifying questions of information presented, stay on topic, and link their own
ideas and understanding to the remarks of others.

88659CAC89024621B5CC20A1F5D230CF.description:
Follow agreed-upon rules for discussions (e.g., gaining the floor in respectful ways, listening to
others with care, speaking one at a time about the topics and texts under discussion).

8E9F8431AA07484BACD3A2BFF4CB4DB3.description:
Come to discussions prepared, having read or studied required material; explicitly draw on that
preparation and other information known about the topic to explore ideas under discussion.

16CEEE6EBFA54993B69455F7424EC170.description:
Engage effectively in a range of collaborative discussions (one-on-one, in groups, and teacher-led) with
diverse partners on grade 3 topics and texts, building on others’ ideas and expressing their own clearly.

BF86259904334D2BAC3BBEC437382459.description:
Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time
frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of discipline-specific tasks, purposes, and
audiences.

37C2EAEAAA0C44D79DC6CEA4D41C5AFB.description:
Recall information from experiences or gather information from print and digital sources; take brief
notes on sources and sort evidence into provided categories.

B7B4B30BAEBE4A539073810C7156C6D9.description: Conduct short research projects that build knowledge about a topic.

19FF6878CB2B4F45A38AEACFAA565EB4.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

84843A849D114BF9864E58EF3C954EA1.description:
With guidance and support from adults, use technology to produce and publish writing (using
keyboarding skills) as well as to interact and collaborate with others.

49C0646BAB734F7EA2F07F47B93E376B.description:
With scaffolding and support from peers and adults, develop and strengthen writing as needed by
planning, revising, and editing. (Editing for conventions should demonstrate command of Language
standards 1–3 up to and including grade 3.)

96BB9FCB691F4D6CA0A7D440E304ED7C.description:
With guidance and support from adults, produce writing in which the development and organization are
appropriate to task and purpose. (Grade-specific expectations for writing types are defined in standards
1–3 above.)

7ACAF2975A9C4A07A340C428CB3A61FA.description: Use temporal words and phrases to signal event order.

1B42C77DDF3F468B85A542682AF1E777.description:
Use dialogue and descriptions of actions, thoughts, and feelings to develop experiences and
events or show the response of characters to situations.

6B10DD4CD8E743558125879098F835EF.description:
Use an organizational structure to establish a situation and introduce a narrator and/or
characters; organize an event sequence that unfolds naturally.

58350C48E35B445E9732E7E5E05EF39C.description:
Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique,
descriptive details, and clear event sequences.

C00933DF97934603B7009D84AE2FB9CF.description: Provide a concluding statement or section.

0DAF44602C5F42719F167F83F47957B3.description:
Use linking words and phrases (e.g., also, another, and, more, but) to connect ideas within
categories of information.

C75529B2DF5E4D38B90DB42A4A323DA4.description: Develop the topic with facts, definitions, and details.

BBF4EF652D344EEE8745B15BDB88C683.description:
Introduce a topic and group related information together; include illustrations when useful to
aiding comprehension.

3AF4ACF8217F44BDBA5B5628AD7CF4C3.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine a topic and convey ideas and information clearly.

42BF57B89EDF4AE4AE3CA500817A7640.description: Provide a concluding statement or section.

FB43F5E144314E82BF537FDD99BFD7CF.description:
Use linking words and phrases (e.g., because, therefore, since, for example) to connect opinion
and reasons.

C808A218C8D6426F8D1A997220FEF557.description: Provide reasons that support the opinion.

4C4D66A111FF4812B9D5B039B46B1B0A.description:
Introduce the topic or text they are writing about, state an opinion, and create an organizational
structure that lists reasons.

CEEA1AD1AF754DC9B1394CA3F6D9388F.description: Write opinion pieces, supporting a point of view with reasons.

C80D43D7B6464FEF984859D848291850.description: Produce cursive writing with accuracy and automaticity.

DD83C20C2FB043EE8E207A4404D8858C.description: Form all upper and lowercase cursive letters efficiently and proportionately.

DC2BB444BE3A4E3EB598398A5F7A0022.description: Write legibly for a variety of tasks and purposes.

4702991B07A24C3CA3ECB2153E8DD468.description:
Read grade-level prose and poetry orally with accuracy, appropriate rate, and expression on
successive readings.

FB6CA111D142440F9B4EB9022256DA12.description: Use decoding skills to self-correct word recognition, rereading as necessary.

1AC67B0AE27440F3A42CCEFC834F69CF.description: Read grade level text with purpose and understanding.

AF3877B7B60E450586AD3A5680AE62E4.description: Read with sufficient accuracy and fluency to support comprehension.

79D05FB733C942F5862F2901207BD836.description: Read grade-appropriate irregularly spelled words with accuracy and automaticity.

970C064CE39D4ED3A9F850A5BB2F1CAD.description: Decode and encode words with common Latin suffixes.

A78827384D2A4118BCCC01AB6A5C3B73.description: Identify and know the meaning of the most common prefixes and derivational suffixes.

4BD4CF1957E842D9BE7AA08AB08BE733.description: Know and apply grade-level phonics and word analysis skills to support decoding and encoding words.

F07656B6D7D54659A62A8F4B33F92B41.description: Reading and Writing Standards: Foundational Skills

9DBDD34ABE15460A8D450495FF0F6106.description:
By the end of the year, read and comprehend informational texts, including history/social studies,
science, and technical texts, at the high end of the grades 2–3 text complexity band independently and
proficiently.

369B1710722A4C44BF67DC46D31073DE.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

BF9A654F0A2146D4B60FDBF0296B90A8.description:
Compare and contrast the most important points and key details presented in two texts on the same
topic.

D87B6C90E5324A76832F8A728EB93E66.description:
Describe the logical connection between particular sentences and paragraphs in a text (e.g.,
comparison, cause/effect, first/second/third in a sequence).

622FF139798C4DA5AD708C79630264E6.description:
Use information gained from illustrations (e.g., maps, photographs) and the words in a text to
demonstrate understanding of the text (e.g., where, when, why, and how key events occur).

B7B8B0CD92C541F4BF9E5674024D7D7F.description: Compare and contrast their own point of view and/or perspective from that of the author of a text.

5985C33912A043EC8A7EFA9BD5FF4C3B.description:
Use text features and search tools (e.g., key words, sidebars, hyperlinks) to locate information relevant
to a given topic efficiently.

23F61AB6344A45959966481D598B2706.description:
Determine the meaning of general academic and domain-specific words and phrases in a text relevant
to a grade 3 topic or subject area.

7D25AEC9FA2A45CFBDE32D14E7194E8C.description:
Describe the relationship between a series of historical events, scientific ideas or concepts, or steps in
technical procedures in a text, using language that pertains to time, sequence, and cause/effect.

37DC04C7E0D54EE89DD70C78152A0C78.description: Determine the main idea of a text; recount the key details and explain how they support the main idea.

FB45863BA0D245FA998E361A886B4A6A.description:
Ask and answer questions to demonstrate understanding of a text, referring explicitly to the text as the
basis for the answers.

23D938C5F2A44F1B846D449D0D38E7CC.description:
By the end of the year, read and comprehend literature, including stories, dramas, and poetry, at the
high end of the grades 2–3 text complexity band independently and proficiently.

E12F6DDA8C5E4B338CE775845F77938C.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

82B3EF7412874EEC9EF4BC222542031E.description:
Compare and contrast the settings, plots, and themes of stories written by the same author about the
same or similar characters (e.g., in books from a series).

A0E35B050A5543B4831B035B6E3504AF.description:
Explain how specific aspects of a text’s illustrations contribute to what is conveyed by the words in a
story (e.g., create mood, emphasize aspects of a character, or setting).

FEA88256BDE24D2A9811C0120A28EB24.description:
Compare and contrast their own point of view (perspective) from that of the narrator or those of the
characters.

FD9E76DD4C02416BA2308BA4AB51490E.description:
Refer to parts of stories, dramas, and poems when writing or speaking about a text, using terms such
as chapter, scene, and stanza; describe how each successive part builds on earlier sections.

62BA8E05D8034BC9BA3232B06CE2AA36.description:
Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, distinguishing literal from
nonliteral language.

F7F3B6807BB445088677F2BCE3B9F12A.description:
Describe characters in a story (e.g., their traits, motivations, or feelings) and explain how their actions
contribute to the sequence of events.

03A034250AFA425C8415482D136A379C.description:
Recount and determine the central message, lesson, or moral of fables, folktales, and myths from
diverse cultures and explain how it is conveyed through key details in the text.

9C852072EEA14B6EA1FE4CC9A2A84BDA.description:
Ask and answer questions to demonstrate understanding of a text, referring explicitly to the text as the
basis for the answers.

standardSets.title: English Language Arts: Grade 4
standardSets.subject: English Language Arts and Literacy in History/Social Studies, Science, and Technical Subjects (2024-)

document.title: Iowa Academic Standards for English Language Arts and Literacy in History/Social Studies, Science, and Technical Subjects

7A89989901E6488FBD81F7B3C4A0782C.description:
Acquire and use accurately grade-appropriate general academic and domain-specific words and
phrases, including those that signal precise actions, emotions, or states of being (e.g., quizzed, whined,
stammered) and that are basic to a particular topic (e.g., wildlife, conservation, and endangered when
discussing animal preservation).

4B0D9CBEA63246D08A869F9F1BA5C42F.description: Demonstrate an understanding of synonyms and antonyms.

E90AF28569CC471CA39733EFB106281D.description: Recognize and explain the meaning of common idioms, adages, and proverbs.

C90CF032C88F450B9861E7BD7818B574.description: Explain the meaning of simple similes and metaphors (e.g., as pretty as a picture) in context.

4F2B9782FC8A4C2CBA5FC8D0F3009814.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

DADF32F2A1C74E30B6AF992450C8C884.description:
Consult reference materials (e.g., dictionaries, glossaries, thesauruses) to find the pronunciation
and determine or clarify the precise meaning of key words and phrases.

B8B0BFAE4EFD4E8691F3E5632539BA6B.description:
Use common, grade-appropriate Greek and Latin affixes and roots as clues to the meaning of a
word (e.g., telegraph, photograph, autograph).

9FC25C0DDF3A4AFAB3D0B1C03DBEFE8B.description:
Use context (e.g., definitions, examples, or restatements in text) as a clue to the meaning of a
word or phrase.

AB9B1B51CF114790B06B954E0AE5DA1D.description:
Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on grade
4 reading and content, choosing flexibly from a range of strategies.

5CD3FBFDC3CE4056BE75481BEA288E97.description:
Differentiate between contexts that call for formal English (e.g., presenting ideas) and situations
where informal discourse is appropriate (e.g., small-group discussion).

6F1CDA45A7F941CC85330851AF19CFD3.description: Choose words and phrases to convey ideas precisely.

266B79A10D83486F979E0599E80C0AE5.description: Use knowledge of language and its conventions when writing, speaking, reading, or listening.

9729E5B1AAE346DB9F4F6576E8CA7DBE.description: Spell correctly, consulting references as needed.

F33119077B2F4A80B04193F438AAA35A.description: Use a comma before a coordinating conjunction in a compound sentence.

A0AC91811A2B4B5CA2E66F173D24DB8F.description: Use commas and quotation marks to mark direct speech and quotations from a text.

6B121DBD5B1348BB961CE2B12866148B.description:
Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling
when writing.

77073BB6CB574BE9989B3CEEE45CD0B6.description: Correctly use homophones (e.g., to, too, two, there, their).

C4ABD81DA2314D449324965C2C847C44.description: Produce complete sentences, recognizing and correcting fragments and run-ons.

CDB83204E5CE424CB24B854C484FF9E7.description: Order adjectives within sentences according to conventional patterns.

4AC64993BE3C4F7CA51148F533D26B92.description: Use modal auxiliaries (e.g., can, may, must) to convey various conditions.

8BFE796F1F4A48B09730A0532DA1F1DB.description: Form and use the progressive (e.g., I was walking; I am walking; I will be walking) verb tenses.

E6D5EBEF60644DEF8342BBA88089A39E.description:
Use relative pronouns (who, whose, whom, which, that) and relative adverbs (where, when,
why).

1D14079992964B259C000805E3F976DE.description:
Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or
speaking.

453C268CFFD7447B9326FD6D8488F52D.description:
Differentiate between contexts that call for formal English (e.g., presenting ideas, performing dramatic
readings or presentations) and situations where informal discourse is appropriate (e.g., small-group
discussion); use formal English when appropriate to task and situation with eye contact, adequate
volume, and clear pronunciation. (See grade 4 Language standards 1 and 3 for specific expectations)

80B1680E75764DDD8FF68180A02D3B40.description:
Add audio recordings and visual displays to presentations when appropriate to enhance the
development of main ideas or themes.

9FD49E133DB84E5887081AE794C47D88.description:
Report on a topic or text, tell a story, or recount an experience in an organized manner, using
appropriate facts and relevant, descriptive details to support main ideas or themes; speak clearly and at
an understandable pace.

E72E03D7F13B494A8E602C41AE0AB7D6.description: Identify the reasons and evidence a speaker provides to support particular points.

A631ADB893CE45F48282F3BA481C8459.description:
Paraphrase text read aloud or information presented in diverse media, and formats, including visually,
quantitatively, and orally.

88458321F5474E1A8F0E4121B45151F6.description:
Review the key ideas expressed and explain their own ideas and understanding in light of the
discussion.

F37060AD0C8647AE99EB5731CD586D8E.description:
Pose and respond to specific questions to clarify or follow up on information, and make
comments that contribute to the discussion and link to the remarks of others.

6B509C67F05B4334B94F51938E17B467.description: Follow agreed-upon rules for discussions and carry out assigned roles.

EFAAD4387E534EC6AA6DCD8862D34B9C.description:
Come to discussions prepared, having read or studied required material; explicitly draw on that
preparation and other information known about the topic to explore ideas under discussion.

E31933C7A56D4B5EAAACC4678ACE1432.description:
Engage effectively in a range of collaborative discussions (one-on-one, in groups, and teacher-led) with
diverse partners on grade 4 topics and texts, building on others’ ideas and expressing their own clearly.

224F8A09D52D4108980DE91B915638DB.description:
Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time
frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of discipline-specific tasks, purposes, and
audiences.

EA0786656F4C41C482DBCFEEA21CBB8C.description:
Apply grade 4 Reading standards to informational texts (e.g., “Explain how an author uses
reasons and evidence to support particular points in a text”).

84706F3BD8DB4436B0B71A7E892C84DD.description:
Apply grade 4 Reading standards to literature (e.g., “Describe in depth a character, setting, or
event in a story or drama, drawing on specific details in the text (e.g., a character’s thoughts,
words, or actions).”).

28C624AFA40B46538C2374AC94EEE098.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

5E900E60598142BB8CF45B756B32597F.description:
Recall relevant information from experiences or gather relevant information from print and digital
sources; take notes and categorize information, and provide a list of sources.

1E4AC7D576B941BCBCE2A825A22F3A55.description:
Conduct short research projects that build knowledge through investigation of different aspects of a
topic.

904EF2BDAAAA434C947243080D6A0556.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

7E2224199FEB41F5814656BA15931306.description:
With some guidance and support from adults, use technology to produce and publish writing as well as
to interact and collaborate with others; demonstrate sufficient command of keyboarding skills.

3A75CDD13CE64BB2A3069D278968C6EF.description:
With guidance and support from peers and adults, develop and strengthen writing as needed by
planning, revising, and editing. (Editing for conventions should demonstrate command of Language
standards 1–3 up to and including grade 4.)

24F289FC099448018FA4D0A59D44D198.description:
Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development and organization are appropriate to task,
purpose, and audience. (Grade-specific expectations for writing types are defined in standards 1–3
above.)

CE67E184E02840C387DA82F51EEF2CD8.description: Provide a conclusion that follows from the narrated experiences or events.

1467186567C144B0ABA2D29D757D5AB9.description:
Use concrete words and phrases and sensory details to convey experiences and events
precisely.

2871C3E52C3E4890BDB5696E40484FAD.description: Use a variety of transitional words and phrases to manage the sequence of events.

3C5266AAFF22417DBFB046E08FAE5114.description:
Use dialogue and description to develop experiences and events or show the responses of
characters to situations.

661D6E55CB9B4D44B30D0012DA35D226.description:
Use an organizational structure to orient the reader by establishing a situation and introducing a
narrator and/or characters; organize an event sequence that unfolds naturally.

231F58E96E05454F80FF4D21063B7CE2.description:
Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique,
descriptive details, and clear event sequences.

6DF733E9FA7A4D40ACEDD482E0A1AA2B.description: Provide a concluding statement or section related to the information or explanation presented.

5A54A9AAF9C84CAB8B2A700B3CA9AAE5.description: Use precise language and domain-specific vocabulary to inform about or explain the topic.

B63FCE3A72644FC58A2CF9D6DCF2C8B2.description:
Link ideas within categories of information using words and phrases (e.g., another, for example,
also, because).

97223FB4BD2146DD8D3A971C3800EA36.description:
Develop the topic with facts, definitions, details, quotations, or other information and examples
related to the topic.

308B5586727A459FB06988E4B44944C9.description:
Introduce a topic clearly and group related information in paragraphs and sections; include
formatting (e.g., headings), illustrations, and multimedia when useful to aiding comprehension.

FE668CAD443C4591A694BAB7E52069C7.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine a topic and convey ideas and information clearly.

CDA9A552B7714CAF867063BC642C2988.description: Provide a concluding statement or section related to the opinion presented.

66969BD3C8EC49D68066CC0B1F88B573.description: Link opinion and reasons using words and phrases (e.g., for instance, in order to, in addition).

1D614F101C314218BDD7F2CC7D9ED8CB.description: Provide reasons that are supported by facts and details.

6309FD6D2BB742D391350F737174C8F2.description:
Introduce a topic or text clearly, state an opinion, and create an organizational structure in which
related ideas are grouped to support the writer’s purpose.

92D0799B750D4508923FB117D30D3814.description: Write an opinion piece, supported by a point of view.

C9DC94C478BD4B259EC399BCF95583D7.description: Apply previous handwriting skills with accuracy and automaticity.

E9CBC3A8AE914028A628DE55553EA466.description: Write legibly for a variety of tasks and purposes.

64821D23DF5A431586FCA9003C19DB38.description:
Orally read grade-level texts (e.g., poetry and prose) with accuracy, automaticity, and expression at an
appropriate rate to support comprehension, self-correcting as necessary.

80A77B685B244A929EECB34D429CA880.description:
Accurately read unfamiliar multisyllabic words in and out of context using sound-spelling
correspondences, syllabication patterns, and morphology (e.g., roots and affixes).

95AE55EC7E874E3F8590263BE14D739F.description: Know and apply grade-level phonics and word analysis skills to support decoding and encoding words.

FCA1A9278F514089B7A11BB3C78012BA.description: Reading and Writing Standards: Foundational Skills

9FB634B363724F5C836FEADCE54BDE7B.description:
By the end of the year, read and comprehend informational texts, including history/social studies,
science, and technical texts, in the grades 4–5 text complexity band proficiently, with scaffolding as
needed at the high end of the range.

0F6D8E9AF7C84DD4B25058BA643F98F5.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

1721AD0D7CB54D4886B49F5DB552B2BD.description:
Integrate information from two texts on the same topic in order to write or speak about the subject
knowledgeably.

520A408AEDE24E2B84526454F8FCF2EA.description: Explain how an author uses reasons and evidence to support particular points in a text.

13738CDF54CD4298824763D584CE3662.description:
Interpret information presented visually, orally, or quantitatively (e.g., in charts, graphs, diagrams, time
lines, animations, or interactive elements on Web pages) and explain how the information contributes to
comprehension of the text.

95CCF1D9561F45B8B2B1EC57B6201035.description:
Compare and contrast a firsthand and secondhand account of the same event or topic; describe the
differences in focus and the information provided.

FB9410158121433598599FE66DD8A0BF.description:
Describe the overall structure (e.g., chronology, comparison, cause/effect, problem/solution) of events,
ideas, concepts, or information in a text or part of a text.

E98DAF0728E741CE9420A8BDA534B572.description:
Determine the meaning of general academic and domain-specific words or phrases in a text relevant to
a grade 4 topic or subject area.

F66C92E0E6BC4D65BE457E5EB71165DD.description:
Explain events, procedures, ideas, or concepts in a historical, scientific, or technical text, including what
happened and why, based on specific details from the text.

3F90B046F98D495CA5BE969B2D950235.description: Determine the main idea of a text and explain how it is supported by key details; summarize the text.

C8962DE5757341A6B946CED7E86D587D.description:
Refer to details and examples in a text when explaining what the text says explicitly and when drawing
inferences from the text.

B3EFC47684004033B7B1BD0A06A7E162.description:
By the end of the year, read and comprehend literature, including stories, dramas, and poetry, in the
grades 4–5 text complexity band proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range.
(RL.4.10)

03D9F4098579471E9E8ED0605F7B446A.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

78AB09D0237B4E898DFD43DEEAB21E93.description:
Compare and contrast the treatment of similar themes and topics (e.g., opposition of good and evil) and
patterns of events (e.g., the quest) in literary text.

78A2C2B89CCE40E99F8A33CE642445FA.description:
Make connections between a literary text and a visual/oral presentation of the text (e.g., mood, aspects
of characters, or setting).

08C874A719184E1E955CD5F685B93C08.description:
Compare and contrast the point of view and/or perspective from which different stories are narrated,
including the difference between first- and third-person narrations.

8056EBD496A64B7DA957883411936304.description:
Explain major differences between poems, drama, and prose, and refer to the structural elements of
poems (e.g., verse, rhythm, meter) and drama (e.g., casts of characters, settings, descriptions,
dialogue, stage directions) when writing or speaking about a text.

AAEC5CB00ADC432A97D68F1CB7A39814.description:
Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including those that allude to
significant characters.

B5CB523EFE944E81A474DFE0DE9A8CCA.description:
Describe in depth a character, setting, or event in a story or drama, drawing on specific details in the
text (e.g., a character’s thoughts, words, or actions).

51D9CC88E139412B9E6A5B2B24DD517B.description: Determine a theme of a story, drama, or poem from details in the text; summarize the text.

ED78C8B3332F41B5A5F3E05FD7826EE8.description:
Refer to details and examples in a text when explaining what the text says explicitly and when drawing
inferences.

standardSets.title: English Language Arts: Grade 5
standardSets.subject: English Language Arts and Literacy in History/Social Studies, Science, and Technical Subjects (2024-)

document.title: Iowa Academic Standards for English Language Arts and Literacy in History/Social Studies, Science, and Technical Subjects

66BA88227ACD4FE3A2D1373D72CC1692.description:
Acquire and use accurately grade-appropriate general academic and domain-specific words and
phrases, including those that signal contrast, addition, and other logical relationships (e.g., however,
although, nevertheless, similarly, moreover, in addition).

4B626E3377074D32AB18C391B945FABE.description:
Use the relationship between particular words (e.g., synonyms, antonyms, homographs) to
better understand each of the words.

B37207C5866240A897393CF528471944.description: Recognize and explain the meaning of common idioms, adages, and proverbs.

C4F1CBB81C344D52A392B36F305432B9.description:
Interpret figurative language, including similes and metaphors (e.g., as pretty as a picture), in
context.

94C07ED3126A45E8BAC522540EB69618.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

5CC490D8DF5D46138A0B7C4C53160D65.description:
Consult reference materials (e.g., dictionaries, glossaries, thesauruses) to find the pronunciation
and determine or clarify the precise meaning of key words and phrases.

CE9F994726EE4A669C8BEC147E7AD1D5.description:
Use common, grade-appropriate Greek and Latin affixes and roots as clues to the meaning of a
word (e.g., photograph, photosynthesis).

83A832B5A8BB4729B691759AE809B15A.description:
Use context (e.g., cause/effect relationships and comparisons in text) as a clue to the meaning
of a word or phrase.

194443D0CDE1417D9C1954993E7E55DE.description:
Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on grade
5 reading and content, choosing flexibly from a range of strategies.

90A7A9BFAC074A8196FFC8A1DDB69164.description: Compare and contrast the varieties of English (e.g., dialects, registers) used in literature.

BEFED27A43174280A87CD67FE5EF34AB.description: Expand, combine, and reduce sentences for meaning, reader/listener interest, and style.

FB0719F7A07A40959487120BED3F2028.description: Use knowledge of language and its conventions when writing, speaking, reading, or listening.

BBFE85A1607D4DB4AB02E8FB4549635E.description: Spell grade-appropriate words correctly, consulting references as needed.

5302F84714234D3089F7C2C81B0C5BE4.description: Use underlining, quotation marks, or italics to indicate titles of works.

6ADD1DD19DD944F48A62CA14E222D337.description:
Use a comma to set off the words yes and no (e.g., Yes, thank you), to set off a tag question
from the rest of the sentence (e.g., It’s true, isn’t it?), and to indicate direct address (e.g., Is that
you, Steve?).

38B0CC40E9184A2E8A4ACABD98F7E406.description: Use a comma to separate an introductory element from the rest of the sentence.

748308445CEA4F1787645D5AEBAC794A.description: Use punctuation to separate items in a series.

B0F9884E5FCC47FCB41296789042DFC5.description:
Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling
when writing.

4B999838C9BB40888ABBFEA706D76B0F.description: Recognize and correct inappropriate shifts in verb tense.

D2F1329395AE45ACB4219A10D01A1630.description: Use verb tense to convey various times, sequences, states, and conditions.

C847F45426604D579DE3F106F19200D0.description: Form and use the perfect (e.g., I had walked; I have walked; I will have walked) verb tenses.

4D973F93E24B427E9AEE32F478EEC271.description:
Explain the function of conjunctions, prepositions, and interjections in general and their function
in particular sentences.

55B342C85947416AB00B614DABFB7863.description:
Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or
speaking.

95A4AE1FD5F5409B8FD6A2DD528B31E8.description:
Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and tasks, using formal English when appropriate to task and
situation, such as when performing dramatic readings or presentations; use appropriate eye contact,
adequate volume, and clear pronunciation. (See grade 5 Language standards 1 and 3 for specific
expectations)

46DA8CF1DB9C4A7C8319F204A565809F.description:
Include multimedia components (e.g., graphics, sound) and visual displays in presentations when
appropriate to enhance the development of main ideas or themes.

32D8B907CA264F40841CF39D60A123FF.description:
Report on a topic or text, or present an opinion, sequencing ideas logically and using appropriate facts
and relevant, descriptive details to support main ideas or themes or central ideas; speak clearly at an
understandable pace.

76BA9E82FC61410BABA16E4F9F7AF193.description:
Summarize the points a speaker makes and explain how each claim is supported by reasons and
evidence.

3E689A5A37894A4AB0714BABD9905BAD.description:
Summarize a written text read aloud or information presented in diverse media and formats, including
visually, quantitatively, and orally.

5F68F9C634924439ABE3E52D1E601B83.description:
Review the key ideas expressed and draw conclusions in light of information and knowledge
gained from the discussions.

C864BE6CFD77436AAD29FDC358AE33A5.description:
Pose and respond to specific questions by making comments that contribute to the discussion
and elaborate on the remarks of others.

A58A579D83164557BB9FFD7940A9C022.description: Follow agreed-upon rules for discussions and carry out assigned roles.

18998FBCE71B440F9C0E02548F61B4B2.description:
Come to discussions prepared, having read or studied required material; explicitly draw on that
preparation and other information known about the topic to explore ideas under discussion.

3217712890CC4399B1BEC140CE8F1D67.description:
Engage effectively in a range of collaborative discussions (one-on-one, in groups, and teacher-led) with
diverse partners on grade 5 topics and texts, building on others’ ideas and expressing their own clearly.

F6E770D2E562458C8318EB0C18BD7460.description:
Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time
frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of discipline-specific tasks, purposes, and
audiences.

4425429768D049F0A452106D15AE08EB.description:
Apply grade 5 Reading standards to informational texts (e.g., “Explain how an author uses
reasons and evidence to support particular points in a text, identifying which reasons and
evidence support which point(s)”).

DE75A3C6E7764380A39250835782CA61.description:
Apply grade 5 Reading standards to literature (e.g., “Compare and contrast stories in the same
genre (e.g., mysteries and adventure stories) on their approaches to similar themes and
topics”).

0922BEE421EE477FB1FA79B0B0600D49.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

9EA1C9B54C9A4878984903F5F0CECBA2.description:
Recall relevant information from experiences or gather relevant information from print and digital
sources; summarize or paraphrase information in notes and finished work, and provide a list of sources.

D1628694CD1544D294F2DDDF22850C24.description:
Conduct short research projects that use several sources to build knowledge through investigation of
different aspects of a topic.

6C7F3483C726473C8922CC1178BB092D.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

176D0BCA94E447AEB2A9BBCF8044EADD.description:
With some guidance and support from adults, use technology to produce and publish writing as well as
to interact and collaborate with others; demonstrate sufficient command of keyboarding skills.

1AF0FBA8482E4D92926957ABEE299660.description:
With guidance and support from peers and adults, develop and strengthen writing as needed by
planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach. (Editing for conventions should
demonstrate command of Language standards 1–3 up to and including grade 5.)

44DC19D2C5DF4284931AF14BF38C1B0C.description:
Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development and organization are appropriate to task,
purpose, and audience. (Grade-specific expectations for writing types are defined in standards 1–3
above.)

4CF206DF7CDF42A1BAB8B5E996B3C658.description: Provide a conclusion that follows from the narrated experiences or events.

9441B525BB124E29B8409B9F48654C9D.description: Use precise words and phrases and sensory details to convey experiences and events.

6DAA9E70BD564860B6B91E2B3AA78B55.description: Use a variety of transitional words, phrases, and clauses to manage the sequence of events.

87C08AA8822843DD830E4A22F0BA8433.description:
Use narrative techniques, such as dialogue, description, and pacing, to develop experiences
and events or show the responses of characters to situations.

88CF9A07C5DE417899FF0D93D4EFA6F9.description:
Use an organizational structure to orient the reader by establishing a situation and introducing a
narrator and/or characters; organize an event sequence that unfolds naturally.

20EF86107FD346F9BB06BB4213C71540.description:
Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique,
descriptive details, and clear event sequences.

7F79F3503AE946D19864F68AE0CD43BD.description: Provide a concluding statement or section related to the information or explanation presented.

669B09026D42498AAE103B80A9031325.description: Use precise language and domain-specific vocabulary to inform about or explain the topic.

424CF1B7E9734C7B9950A5868EC9729E.description:
Link ideas within and across categories of information using words, phrases, and clauses (e.g.,
in contrast, especially).

EACE6EFF91A24B95BC4E2BA317DE930B.description:
Develop the topic with facts, definitions, concrete details, quotations, or other information and
examples related to the topic.

A9F92E86CA504EE9A98577001D09DA97.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine a topic and convey ideas and information clearly.

DB9CE2DF3B8D4B21BB82E19F03C529BD.description: Provide a concluding statement or section related to the opinion presented.

FA8C8E023B734E598C15B4DE23AAEB8C.description: Link opinion and reasons using words, phrases, and clauses (e.g., consequently, specifically).

D031A38F73704596AC5292B9326F4CC7.description: Provide logically ordered reasons that are supported by facts and details.

98C72E8C8F7F49E0B83B0CE1AFFE009F.description:
Introduce a topic or text clearly, state an opinion, and create an organizational structure in which
ideas are logically grouped to support the writer’s purpose.

4B8A823B19CE4DB39B730CC083F7C27A.description: Write opinion pieces that explain a perspective or point of view with supporting reasons and evidence.

610CF1BAB59D4F379D329C92D76AF3D2.description: Apply previous handwriting skills with accuracy and automaticity.

CB20FB91D5E84A9F85F6B13E40B8D6CE.description: Write legibly for a variety of tasks and purposes.

D9ED3E8B22754FE38A68A9B8E84899AA.description:
Orally read grade-level texts (e.g., poetry and prose) with accuracy, automaticity, and expression at an
appropriate rate to support comprehension, self-correcting as necessary.

546F9EC99C0448AC849AACC95DE086EB.description:
Accurately read unfamiliar multisyllabic words in and out of context using combined knowledge
of all sound-spelling correspondences, syllabication patterns and morphology (e.g., roots and
affixes).

BDC59A2001B14C0C8F2AE7564026CC2A.description: Know and apply grade-level phonics and word analysis skills to support decoding and encoding words.

895BDC4132ED4403B88DEB43AB1EAA40.description: Reading and Writing Standards: Foundational Skills

4BE42DF7935248A1A61700D5431B1C12.description:
By the end of the year, read and comprehend informational texts, including history/social studies,
science, and technical texts, at the high end of the grades 4–5 text complexity band independently and
proficiently.

710E0B0C146E40A0815F059776E11C2D.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

E7BD7AFD9FCB4117B0C4E7A8E5C197CA.description:
Integrate information from several texts on the same topic in order to write or speak about the subject
knowledgeably.

7BAC69E2C1134BFBBC02EC13BB1DC6DB.description:
Explain how an author uses reasons and evidence to support particular points in a text, identifying
which reasons and evidence support which point(s).

5007ACE8E7D54BFB8981B91F5E6A2689.description:
Draw on information from multiple print or digital sources, demonstrating the ability to locate an answer
to a question or to solve a problem.

364C3D59910B4DCBBED7C7035E96A5AA.description:
Analyze multiple accounts of the same event or topic, noting important similarities and differences in
the point of view they represent.

641E2080774E4091BBFCF22E97580DB5.description:
Compare and contrast the overall structure (e.g., chronology, comparison, cause/effect,
problem/solution) of events, ideas, concepts, or information in two or more texts.

3D67BB5BF15C48019109B48C2C149EB6.description:
Determine the meaning of general academic and domain-specific words and phrases in a text relevant
to a grade 5 topic or subject area.

FA7851A187C64E08A1A536264BDD85C8.description:
Explain the relationships or interactions between two or more individuals, events, ideas, or concepts in
a historical, scientific and/or technical text based on specific information in the text(s).

B8B722DF63D1462E8ABF185690817017.description:
Determine two or more main ideas of a text and explain how they are supported by key details;
summarize the text.

216902F3DF0144E0BE919D512B225AFB.description:
Quote accurately from a text when explaining what the text says explicitly and when drawing
inferences.

CE7DB5CB19674E72A08C02169653444B.description:
By the end of the year, read and comprehend literature, including stories, dramas, and poetry, at the
high end of the grades 4–5 text complexity band independently and proficiently.

CDF269D51EFC433BAD4077E67624885B.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

7AB8DED9231D47AC9A3B062B0FEC1F48.description:
Compare and contrast stories in the same genre (e.g., mysteries and adventure stories) on their
approaches to similar themes and topics.

C0BA33082999443CB91A38A69FB136AF.description:
Analyze how visual and multimedia elements contribute to the meaning, tone, or mood of a text (e.g.,
graphic novel, multimedia presentation of fiction, folktale, myth, poem).

97F4FAA0FF454A138594580DF8A25235.description:
Describe how a narrator’s or speaker’s point of view and/or perspective influences how events are
described.

2D669987044D433C9A9A845E0422F130.description:
Explain how a series of chapters, scenes, or stanzas fit together to provide the overall structure of a
particular story, drama, or poem.

CB68F46AB066441F9D2EE7B806CB7CBF.description:
Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including figurative language
such as metaphors and similes.

318C36AB58F34AA1B11A6B5EF82EE0E9.description:
Compare and contrast two or more characters, settings, or events in a story or drama, drawing on
specific details in the text (e.g., how characters interact).

CADC4D9DEC7945C78464CF13B3D43F65.description:
Determine a theme of a story, drama, or poem from details in the text, including how characters in a
story or drama respond to challenges or how the speaker in a poem reflects upon a topic; summarize
the text.

676B063B8AD34D1589B9FC7D5E4EF2BF.description:
Quote accurately from a text when explaining what the text says explicitly and when drawing
inferences.

standardSets.title: English Language Arts: Grade 6
standardSets.subject: English Language Arts and Literacy in History/Social Studies, Science, and Technical Subjects (2024-)

document.title: Iowa Academic Standards for English Language Arts and Literacy in History/Social Studies, Science, and Technical Subjects

093327EDD8DC43DFBFFD04D98533B3AC.description:
Acquire and use accurately grade-appropriate general academic and domain-specific words and
phrases; gather vocabulary knowledge when considering a word or phrase important to comprehension
or expression.

FC7BA18E1D804116B7902CDD169926B2.description:
Distinguish among the connotations (associations) of words with similar denotations (definitions)
(e.g., stingy, scrimping, economical, unwasteful, thrifty).

9F10F522670D4C6EB98F2064D4EB657E.description:
Use the relationship between particular words (e.g., cause/effect, part/whole, item/category) to
better understand each of the words.

E59D20A7B1304396B8C6B5CF0C344D07.description: Interpret figures of speech (e.g., personification, hyperbole) in context.

10C57EB070384743B06CD2E83703E507.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

BDD14FECBBB24738815C09372E0DCC16.description:
Verify the preliminary determination of the meaning of a word or phrase (e.g., by checking the
inferred meaning in context or by using other reference materials).

8CC989F4E3964753AE8CBCC7F82548BB.description:
Consult reference materials (e.g., dictionaries, glossaries, thesauruses) to find the pronunciation
of a word or determine or clarify its precise meaning or its part of speech.

6D24B870400948B2AD81850524D2DF25.description:
Use common, grade-appropriate Greek or Latin affixes and roots as clues to the meaning of a
word (e.g., audience, auditory, audible).

4563F6BB453A40FFAE93B2EC19E6198E.description:
Use context (e.g., the overall meaning of a sentence or paragraph; a word’s position or function
in a sentence) as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.

B73B93AE90844CE6B6525AF2A1AA8C68.description:
Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on grade
6 reading and content, choosing flexibly from a range of strategies.

B2CC2F969ED2456D906241660CEA6BED.description: Maintain consistency in style and tone.

C999D329F0D84396A76CB098FD11A906.description: Vary sentence patterns for meaning, reader/listener interest, and style.

A469DA16DD904B45B7F090725A3AF2AD.description: Use knowledge of language and its conventions when writing, speaking, reading, or listening.

F869C835D1B247FB9F79C3DAAE37F33D.description: Spell correctly, consulting references as needed.

E0509B16C414408B875CBFAC165CD385.description:
Use punctuation (commas, parentheses, dashes) to set off nonrestrictive/parenthetical
elements.

863EF59B0F7440D2A4ADBE97200DDD51.description:
Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling
when writing.

71165C897BE24E0F9D4F8CFA75AF2BFE.description:
Recognize variations from standard English in their own and others’ writing and speaking, and
identify and use strategies to improve expression in conventional language.

F02E25E36CDF4F9093173F56E2BD87B1.description: Recognize and correct vague pronouns (i.e., ones with unclear or ambiguous antecedents).

4D5A5FAE709A43ABA029555B8A87381E.description: Recognize and correct inappropriate shifts in pronoun number and person.

C1CBA6C5DE55438497B4C2A88F370E29.description: Use pronouns in the proper case (subjective, objective, possessive).

B0DE74EA3C474CEBBBD30549FE7A8DDD.description:
Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or
speaking.

99082670FA554A778D26F92C6277F518.description:
Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and tasks, such as conducting interviews and participating in
public performances, demonstrating command of formal English when indicated or appropriate; use
appropriate eye contact, adequate volume, and clear pronunciation. (See grade 6 Language standards
1 and 3 for specific expectations)

4F5906E12FEB46D7915106AA9E6C7239.description:
Include multimedia components (e.g., graphics, images, music, sound) and visual displays in
presentations to clarify information.

C874D504B60C41A2B9FB8DB708EC336A.description:
Present claims and findings, sequencing ideas logically and using pertinent descriptions, facts, and
details to accentuate main ideas or themes appropriate to purpose, audience, and task.

19C32377CA7A4BC28EA39086DC122A7D.description:
Delineate a speaker’s argument and specific claims, distinguishing claims that are supported by
reasons and evidence from claims that are not.

46A4A49278974C18BE047AAC4A533693.description:
