572587E1D2BD44FC9754C93F09601469.description:
Use common, grade-appropriate Greek or Latin affixes and roots as clues to the meaning of a
word (e.g., precede, recede, secede).

64B2A0D6AABC42989053F567B4344630.description:
Use context (e.g., the overall meaning of a sentence or paragraph; a word’s position or function
in a sentence) as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.

1E6F6380900F48CB96B0703203A71412.description:
Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words or phrases based on grade 8
reading and content, choosing flexibly from a range of strategies.

F85723B67E07448B94D54327644C7FEF.description:
Use verbs in the active or passive voice and in the conditional and subjunctive mood to achieve
particular effects (e.g., emphasizing the actor or the action; expressing uncertainty or describing
a state contrary to fact).

DE2EEFC250314EE5B9FEC0F040218246.description: Apply knowledge of language and its conventions when writing, speaking, reading, or listening.

9928FA540FCB441CAA1EDBE92C3782FB.description: Spell correctly, consulting references as needed.

12DAD3956EE34D7E8F5C7ED9081C8426.description: Use an ellipsis to indicate an omission.

800B992C7DF04CCBBFE76B4450195300.description: Use punctuation (comma, ellipsis, dash) to indicate a pause or break.

28ADB84563AF4E5FBE97510EB8A169BB.description:
Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling
when writing.

ED2556ECC78D40578A9BD6EC60347BC6.description: Recognize and correct inappropriate shifts in verb voice and mood.

B61862D9D9684F5199C94C55C07FF81D.description:
Form and use verbs in the indicative, imperative, interrogative, conditional, and subjunctive
mood.

123FC97FAC7B42CBB0187170FF85AA66.description: Form and use verbs in the active and passive voice.

B8BF04F485084F84A61C1A2298EF7EFE.description:
Explain the function of verbals (gerunds, participles, infinitives) in general and their function in
particular sentences.

735A9DB09FC14792A422F7D3E8380486.description:
Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or
speaking.

D657843CB0704C67AE00F8C37B0728D7.description:
Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and tasks, such as conducting interviews and participating in
public performances, demonstrating command of formal English when indicated or appropriate; use
appropriate eye contact, adequate volume, and clear pronunciation. (See grade 8 Language standards
1 and 3 for specific expectations)

82EF51B580034F8C86A6AC213F5F8AB1.description:
Integrate multimedia components and visual displays (e.g., graphics, images, charts and graphs,
sound, audio, interactive elements) in presentations to clarify information, strengthen claims and
evidence, and add interest.

D5364CF41E354AED945DE1F5B67D2C7A.description:
Present claims and findings, emphasizing salient points in a focused, coherent manner with relevant
evidence, sound valid reasoning, and well-chosen details appropriate to the purpose, audience, and
task.

9AC747D60D0343399C1B8C4A79F639AE.description:
Delineate a speaker’s argument and specific claims, evaluating the soundness of the reasoning and
relevance and sufficiency of the evidence, and identifying when irrelevant evidence is introduced.

E480A683DD5B4BF2B29FA6F79469F831.description:
Analyze the purpose of information presented in diverse media and formats (e.g., visually,
quantitatively, orally) and evaluate the motives (e.g., social, commercial, political) behind its
presentation.

533A0B77061546518F98A18DB83B9C21.description:
Acknowledge new information expressed by others, and, when warranted, justify or modify their
own views in light of the evidence presented.

F2F90737169D45DE97F0B2A6CFF739FA.description:
Pose questions that connect the ideas of several speakers and respond to others’ questions
and comments with relevant evidence, observations, and ideas.

8B2017C533EB48D383961C615DD753D0.description:
Follow rules for collegial discussions and decision-making (e.g., informal consensus, taking
votes on key issues, presentation of alternate views), track progress toward specific goals and
deadlines, and define individual roles as needed.

CE2677251BDE4931B313A0A0220B1667.description:
Come to discussions prepared, having read or researched material under study; explicitly draw
on that preparation by referring to evidence on the topic, text, or issue to probe and reflect on
ideas under discussion.

8BB431A5C85D4352A98234FF1BF98A83.description:
Engage effectively in a range of collaborative discussions (one-on-one, in groups, and teacher-led) with
diverse partners on grade 8 topics, texts, and issues, building on others’ ideas and expressing their
own clearly.

E1323F0A122443F88332B4F0A54B43D0.description:
Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time
frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of discipline-specific tasks, purposes, and
audiences.

93AE34DBC3D843898307A578B8BF56D1.description:
Apply grade 8 Reading standards to literary nonfiction (e.g., “Delineate and evaluate the
argument and specific claims in a text, assessing whether the reasoning is sound and the
evidence is relevant and sufficient; recognize when irrelevant evidence is introduced”).

DD55FC3DE9874D5188814C0617860793.description:
Apply grade 8 Reading standards to literature (e.g., “Analyze how a modern work of fiction
draws on themes, patterns of events, or character types from myths, traditional stories, or
religious works, including describing how the material is rendered new”).

4C548FBC9CE0413AAD1B8A49ABC6E081.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

42BC82421B7F46AFBDFF8471926D9BB5.description:
Conduct short research projects to answer a question (including a self-generated question), drawing on
several sources and generating additional related, focused questions that allow for multiple avenues of
exploration.

7C5F1012F621445397F84C4EB0CA7A6A.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

AA28984B096E4C7CB552C1EC35C5D26D.description:
Use technology to produce and publish writing to interact and collaborate with others through a variety
of media to present the relationships between information and ideas efficiently, including linking to and
citing sources.

B892CED19F074A10BDF61227BB94B6A3.description:
With some guidance and support from peers and adults, develop and strengthen writing as needed by
planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach, focusing on how well purpose and
audience have been addressed. (Editing for conventions should demonstrate command of Language
standards 1–3 up to and including grade 8.)

84240112A38B46E58DD3D748F66C871F.description:
Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to
task, purpose, and audience. (Grade-specific expectations for writing types are defined in standards 1–
3 above.)

631EE3C3778D4D0F8C318550F49D940E.description: Provide a conclusion that follows and reflects on the narrated experiences or events.

BB0F02756BFD4B0E8A21F36E1942098A.description:
Use precise words and phrases, relevant descriptive details, and sensory language to capture
the action and convey experiences and events.

9A9C8D3025BD4C779AD87E9926D153CF.description:
Use a variety of transition words, phrases, and clauses to convey sequence, signal shifts from
one time frame or setting to another, and show the relationships among experiences and
events.

88410D7D794A41389F9BF17D170E2C7D.description:
Use narrative techniques, such as dialogue, pacing, description, and reflection, to develop
experiences, events, and/or characters.

8784FFF6C8DA41EEA435F98AA5994E39.description:
Engage and orient the reader by establishing a context and point of view and introducing a
narrator and/or characters; organize an event sequence that unfolds naturally and logically.

8E208B1458A84BE1A1ECBCD82643E900.description:
Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, relevant
descriptive details, and well-structured event sequences.

7B4BD31F39474A7A821B610D4B0EC6E2.description:
Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the information or
explanation presented.

27C120141F004B3691712E30C178FC25.description: Establish and maintain a formal style.

8FAC51BBEB9F4F7089656EA55D5FDCDC.description: Use precise language and domain-specific vocabulary to inform about or explain the topic.

A66471DE3EB741DF9255F11E37AA6399.description:
Use appropriate and varied transitions to create cohesion and clarify the relationships among
ideas and concepts.

71311B7895B34DFE9B6C1DADBEEAD27B.description:
Develop the topic with relevant, well-chosen facts, definitions, concrete details, quotations, or
other information and examples.

67008D2DF8F8470388113F90543AA2F7.description:
Introduce a topic clearly, previewing what is to follow; organize ideas, concepts, and information
into broader categories; include formatting (e.g., headings), graphics (e.g., charts, tables), and
multimedia when useful to aiding comprehension.

62769E090FF1428BBB2E1757B801795B.description:
Write informative/explanatory texts to examine a topic and convey ideas, concepts, and information
through the selection, organization, and analysis of relevant content.

6B7D9573C390466A96690AE3D4902674.description: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows and supports the argument presented.

91DF1ED400A5466D86F9B0167B1C2DC5.description: Establish and maintain a tone and style appropriate to the task and audience.

FE951AAB2AFE446987EEF9467028F4F8.description:
Use words, phrases, and clauses to create cohesion and clarify the relationships among
claim(s), counterclaims, reasons, and evidence.

57D590DEF2634362AA46E77E108A2956.description:
Support claim(s) with logical reasoning and relevant evidence, using accurate, credible sources
and demonstrating an understanding of the topic or text.

6E6E748BF12942E88B7D7F276B9B5F8D.description:
Introduce claim(s), acknowledge and distinguish the claim(s) from alternate or opposing claims,
and organize the reasons and evidence logically.

DABAC7D31113412283E341CC80B1F9E1.description: Write arguments to support claims with clear reasons and relevant evidence.

B456A0AFF7B5408CABAA735E8EB51851.description:
By the end of the year, read and comprehend literary nonfiction, at the high end of the grades 6-8 text
complexity band independently and proficiently.

5081482D705344F8B247B99A68A00E0A.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

F19DDB8C0DBA4F409FE07F1E81BCE22F.description:
Analyze how two or more texts provide conflicting information on the same topic and identify where the
texts disagree on matters of fact or interpretation.

D7E768B565C84656AED0E5630FF971F7.description:
Delineate and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, assessing whether the reasoning is
sound and the evidence is relevant and sufficient; recognize when irrelevant evidence is introduced.

62E30B3D7D514080BCB20BF0E186C568.description:
Evaluate the advantages and disadvantages of using different mediums (e.g., print or digital text, video,
multimedia) to present a particular topic or idea.

A335A87E31FB4F5AB72079BA24862008.description:
Determine an author’s point of view or purpose in a text and analyze how the author acknowledges and
responds to conflicting evidence or viewpoints.

1B3BBCFACC234BF8B07196B592FFD8B4.description:
Analyze in detail the structure of a specific paragraph in a text, including the role of particular sentences
in developing and refining a key concept.

707C0FAB3A6545C2A081FC70F9A2EEC0.description:
Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including figurative,
connotative, and technical meanings; analyze the impact of specific word choices and phrases on
meaning and tone, including analogies or allusions to other texts.

FF9ED508232F4CECB96BAF51B18B8099.description:
Analyze how a text makes connections among and distinctions between individuals, ideas, or events
(e.g., through comparisons, analogies, or categories).

7E264CD73308464BAA8CF80EFFC1D5E7.description: Incorporate central ideas and their relationships into an objective summary of the text.

FD04AABD7E99449E9AEC6DE632526FF3.description:
Determine a central idea of a text and analyze its development over the course of the text,
including its relationship to supporting ideas.

65539A5C4A474365B253DB82F3BC0AA1.description:
Cite the textual evidence that most strongly supports an analysis of what the text says explicitly as well
as inferences drawn from the text.

32B87B61619C4F3BBE842DE2CB6A6C77.description:
By the end of the year, read and comprehend literature, including stories, dramas, and poems, at the
high end of grades 6-8 complexity band independently and proficiently.

1427D07CAC674D64B5A636BC1C42EA70.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

436F11B8E13842B3AFC39D3B8F80D771.description:
Analyze how a modern work of fiction draws on themes, patterns of events, or character types from
myths, traditional stories, or religious works, including describing how the material is rendered new.

3A6149FE8F59469EA4DC9DBF25EC8126.description:
Analyze the extent to which a filmed or live production of a story or drama stays faithful to or departs
from the text or script, evaluating the choices made by the director or actors.

039E8FABB34749BF9F854C570092EFDC.description:
Analyze how differences in point of view and/or perspectives of the characters and the audience or
reader (e.g., created through the use of dramatic irony) create such effects as suspense or humor.

02C736ED60B04FF8A7AE4CFD26D62549.description:
Compare and contrast the structure of two or more texts and analyze how the differing structure of each
text contributes to its meaning and style.

7E68BE91E13B4CDF85423825FC6BCC55.description:
Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including figurative and
connotative meanings; analyze the impact of specific word choices on meaning and tone, including
analogies or allusions to other texts.

252C3B5482F44577BCA0F0CE542E6A09.description:
Analyze how particular lines of dialogue or incidents in a story or drama propel the action, reveal
aspects of a character, or provoke a decision.

804A10EBBC32473DBC7D10DA94860E08.description:
Incorporate a theme and its relationship to other story elements into an objective summary of
the text.

519BA03A14824FEA8095B83BD09EB18E.description:
Determine a theme of a text and analyze its development over the course of the text, including
its relationship to the characters, setting, and plot.

D0D4631ACE2B4C6189F051261FD81C0F.description:
Cite the textual evidence that most strongly supports an analysis of what the text says explicitly as well
as inferences drawn from the text.

standardSets.title: English Language Arts: Grades 9-10
standardSets.subject: English Language Arts and Literacy in History/Social Studies, Science, and Technical Subjects (2024-)

document.title: Iowa Academic Standards for English Language Arts and Literacy in History/Social Studies, Science, and Technical Subjects

353D75B07C0C4B1D9789AA8FC16CF07B.description:
Acquire and use accurately general academic and domain-specific words and phrases, sufficient for
reading, writing, speaking, and listening at the college and career readiness level; demonstrate
independence in gathering vocabulary knowledge when considering a word or phrase important to
comprehension or expression.

29D21262DDEE4253A1EB431FC5CFC7CF.description: Analyze nuances in the meaning of words with similar denotations.

8870EF187D0E4098BF34362C06CEDA8B.description:
Interpret figures of speech (e.g., euphemism, oxymoron, verbal irony, satire, idiom, paradox) in
context and analyze their role in the text.

A253796B07BE4593BF4A3B4764852067.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

31AF7D34989143529BF8F477FD0E1533.description:
Verify the preliminary determination of the meaning of a word or phrase (e.g., by checking the
inferred meaning in context or by using other reference materials).

F053004FD8694F3F95AC4495D5C7F302.description:
Consult general and specialized reference materials (e.g., dictionaries, glossaries,
thesauruses), both print and digital, to find the pronunciation of a word or determine or clarify its
precise meaning, its part of speech, or its etymology.

FC1029C1E9974DA9B37BAF18D851BB33.description:
Identify and correctly use patterns of word changes that indicate different meanings or parts of
speech (e.g., analyze, analysis, analytical; advocate, advocacy).

D131587364084182BF670FF923CAB9D2.description:
Use context (e.g., the overall meaning of a sentence, paragraph, or text; a word’s position or
function in a sentence) as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.

640F9383E5444CA8BC18C9747D59D041.description:
Use a variety of strategies to determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words
and phrases based on grades 9–10 reading and content.

2761AE09B9C84F749788E19A1011CB05.description:
Write and edit work so that it conforms to the guidelines in a style manual (e.g., MLA Handbook,
APA Style) appropriate for the discipline and writing type.

4DE893F292204E87945AB07D36CEBC09.description:
Apply knowledge of language to understand how language functions in different contexts, to make
effective choices for meaning or style, and to comprehend more fully when reading or listening.

9733E681C9884B3EB193D7D602DCB892.description: Spell correctly, consulting references as needed.

4D5998F993264A01A33378BB4332F564.description: Use a colon to introduce a list or quotation.

D906A4F4A0C847ABA5E82D58304C6C9D.description:
Use a semicolon (and perhaps a conjunctive adverb) to link two or more closely related
independent clauses.

716A6268CA904F798A9D99A61087C761.description:
Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling
when writing.

87DE7641FB5A46B38007BBF3BF5EDD05.description:
Use various types of phrases (noun, verb, adjectival, adverbial, participial, prepositional,
absolute) and clauses (independent, dependent; noun, relative, adverbial) to convey specific
meanings and add variety and interest to writing or presentations.

86F1E557D82E42E5B9BF152A112E0781.description:
Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or
speaking.

89FF2991303F4F39AE87EB477ADF21D1.description:
Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and tasks, such as conducting interviews, participating in public
performances, or debating an issue from either side, demonstrating command of formal English when
indicated or appropriate; use appropriate eye contact, adequate volume, and clear pronunciation. (See
grades 9–10 Language standards 1 and 3 for specific expectations)

3AA1AD26775742D48356BA010493AFA5.description:
Make strategic use of digital media (e.g., textual, graphical, audio, visual, and interactive elements) in
presentations to enhance understanding of findings, reasoning, and evidence and to add interest.

C4051E2EBD92412AAB2A3EA56D933648.description:
Present information, findings, and supporting evidence clearly, concisely, and logically such that
listeners can follow the line of reasoning and the organization, development, substance, and style are
appropriate to purpose, audience, and task.

F39508B65D444DF0B8C7734DDB554A34.description:
Evaluate a speaker’s point of view (perspective), reasoning, and use of evidence and rhetoric,
identifying any fallacious reasoning or exaggerated or distorted evidence.

899E739EF52D44CB99C521842F072FE4.description:
Integrate multiple sources of information presented in diverse media or formats (e.g., visually,
quantitatively, orally), evaluating the credibility and accuracy of each source.

5F13EBC88B4144718A9EE57749B58A77.description:
Respond thoughtfully to diverse perspectives, summarize points of agreement and
disagreement, and, when warranted, qualify or justify their own views and understanding and
make new connections in light of the evidence and reasoning presented.

1A41D2ABA70A48A8B9609F8DAE64EBE5.description:
Propel conversations by posing and responding to questions that relate the current discussion
to broader themes or larger ideas; actively incorporate others into the discussion; and clarify,
verify, or challenge ideas and conclusions.

071068E09E7C429D9B6F1E0CE1D7E434.description:
Work with peers to set rules for collegial discussions and decision-making (e.g., informal
consensus, taking votes on key issues, presentation of alternate views), clear goals and
deadlines, and individual roles as needed.

967FBE81E8CC497BB66C0F488099A874.description:
Come to discussions prepared, having read and researched material under study; explicitly
draw on that preparation by referring to evidence from texts and other research on the topic or
issue to stimulate a thoughtful, well-reasoned exchange of ideas.

59CA43335A6041F0BB06A11D5410E931.description:
Initiate and participate effectively in a range of collaborative discussions (one-on-one, in groups, and
teacher-led) with diverse partners on grades 9–10 topics, texts, and issues, building on others’ ideas
and expressing their own clearly and persuasively.

ED7D23B73AA8425CA03B3FA928B2D507.description:
Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time
frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of tasks, purposes, and audiences, scaffolding as
needed.

9654DC79FEE6485E8B625485A4C17A0F.description:
Apply grades 9–10 Reading standards to literary nonfiction (e.g., “Delineate and evaluate the
argument and specific claims in a text, assessing whether the reasoning is valid and the
evidence is relevant and sufficient; identify any false statements and fallacious reasoning”).

D8372DFBDBFF4D3B82A903063997D8D2.description:
Apply grades 9–10 Reading standards to literature (e.g., “Analyze how an author draws on and
transforms source material in a specific work.”).

F03F3CFCF10C493E976F653CA4ACC7D1.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

1D85DA7CE9334EF095011E808D075933.description:
Gather relevant information from multiple credible primary and secondary authoritative print and digital
sources, using advanced searches effectively; assess the usefulness of each source in answering the
research question; integrate information into the text selectively to maintain the flow of ideas, avoiding
plagiarism and following a standard format for citation.

14FB6A652B8745799A961F108DDE5534.description:
Conduct short as well as more sustained research projects to answer a question (including a selfgenerated question) or solve a problem; narrow or broaden the inquiry when appropriate; synthesize
multiple sources on the subject, demonstrating understanding of the subject under investigation.

B3D2102E69574D6293F18DE101E1F0AA.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

A190814DDBE64A31B3E42949CC033680.description:
Use technology to produce, publish, and update individual or shared writing products, taking advantage
of technology’s capacity to link to other information and to display information flexibly and dynamically.

393BD5751FFD42119FF8959395A02FEF.description:
Develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new
approach, focusing on addressing what is most significant for a specific purpose and audience. (Editing
for conventions should demonstrate command of Language standards 1–3 up to and including grades
9–10.)

9BE08A5B96AD4970BCE8479703AAB5CE.description:
Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to
task, purpose, and audience. (Grade-specific expectations for writing types are defined in standards 1–
3 above).

662B377AD52D4CECA4B0C600565C231B.description:
Provide a conclusion that follows from and reflects on what is experienced, observed, or
resolved over the course of the narrative.

E6DE80BB577D408AA8A060B95050F07E.description:
Use precise words and phrases, telling details, and sensory language to convey a vivid picture
of the experiences, events, setting, and/or characters.

6C46AB6C2C85431399C811E7FFC79694.description:
Use a variety of techniques to sequence events so that they build on one another to create a
coherent whole (e.g., flashback, foreshadowing, and cause and effect).

589C5CD313C442C0A15766523DCAC25F.description:
Use narrative techniques, including dialogue, pacing, description, reflection, and multiple plot
lines, to develop experiences, events, and/or characters; create a smooth progression of
experiences or events.

A3424A100A9444D5883D36ED4DF88CEA.description:
Engage and orient the reader by setting out a problem, situation, or observation and its
significance, establishing one or multiple point(s) of view, and introducing a narrator and/or
characters.

F5358616E44A412CBD40405455CCD3E0.description: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, well-chosen details, and well-structured event sequences.

2A19AACD9BA843629886A7EB7856EF41.description:
Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the information or
explanation presented (e.g., articulating implications or the significance of the topic).

314F87E44E4E49DFADB5CDFB4B47042B.description:
Establish and maintain a formal style and objective tone while attending to the norms and
conventions of the discipline in which they are writing.

4E18D36D944940A3B07B9FED4E948D98.description: Use precise language and domain-specific vocabulary to manage the complexity of the topic.

BA7BAD0334884196ABFB14069DBF939B.description:
Use appropriate and varied transitions to link the major sections of the text, create cohesion,
and clarify the relationships among complex ideas and concepts.

7010C2649FE7442E92AEACC309391F32.description:
Develop the topic with well-chosen, relevant, and sufficient facts, extended definitions, concrete
details, quotations, or other information and examples appropriate to the audience’s knowledge
of the topic.

42FBC2CE636E45EB8DAFD366C548CBEA.description:
Introduce a topic; organize complex ideas, concepts, and information to make important
connections and distinctions; include formatting (e.g., headings), graphics (e.g., figures, tables),
and multimedia when useful to aiding comprehension.

8212EE535FB14C14AA3478F7E55F98B1.description:
Write informative/explanatory texts to examine and convey complex ideas, concepts, and information
clearly and accurately through the effective selection, organization, and analysis of content.

023272C03F224195880630F7E4F35E3C.description:
Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the argument
presented.

592D93B47434413F80220048C1911250.description:
Establish and maintain a formal style and objective tone while attending to the norms and
conventions of the discipline in which they are writing.

652D2B1EB0C14ED8A2F40F9EA08EA4F5.description:
Use words, phrases, and clauses to link the major sections of the text, create cohesion, and
clarify the relationships between claim(s) and reasons, between reasons and evidence, and
between claim(s) and counterclaims.

33F4F988101341CB83EE27E053C70DF3.description:
Develop claim(s) and counterclaims fairly, supplying evidence for each while pointing out the
strengths and limitations of both in a manner that anticipates the audience’s knowledge level
and concerns.

84F24E4897984069A227449483668632.description:
Introduce precise claim(s), distinguish the claim(s) from alternate or opposing claims, and create
an organization that establishes clear relationships among claim(s), counterclaims, reasons,
and evidence.

900EC2CE5EA040DA9E29C903DCEF9CDA.description:
Write arguments to support claims in an analysis of substantive topics or texts, using valid reasoning
and relevant and sufficient evidence.

64FC6CA0DE8D4C71AA7E28547D7C76B8.description:
By the end of grade 9, read and comprehend literary nonfiction in the grades 9–10 text complexity band
proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range.
By the end of grade 10, read and comprehend literary nonfiction at the high end of the grades 9–10 text
complexity band independently and proficiently.

86A6BDAA6D6B4C3F8570A2E4C7D07E2B.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

363D03BD737D4BE499B128C159B946EB.description:
Analyze seminal U.S. documents of historical and literary significance, including how they address
related themes and concepts.

B3999FF3D3914401B69CE64293697B55.description:
Delineate and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, assessing whether the reasoning is
valid and the evidence is relevant and sufficient; identify any false statements and fallacious reasoning.

4235DC54AA8D4E2B8C44AA904C4C7170.description:
Analyze various accounts of a subject told in different mediums (e.g., a person’s life story in both print
and multimedia), determining which details are emphasized in each account.

28FAEA4C807140279784833496A455D0.description:
Determine an author’s point of view or purpose in a text and analyze how an author uses rhetoric to
advance that point of view or purpose.

73D777081CFF499CAD50B398322CA9BB.description:
Analyze in detail how an author’s ideas or claims are developed by particular sentences, paragraphs, or
larger portions of a text (e.g., a section or chapter).

A9EFD073F9F748A9A9E49FAED9913BEC.description:
Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including figurative,
connotative, and technical meanings; analyze the cumulative impact of specific word choices on
meaning and tone (e.g., how the language of a court opinion differs from that of a newspaper).

16673A2671144270A8D9D056F76B3576.description:
Analyze how the author unfolds an analysis or series of ideas or events, including the order in which
the points are made, how they are introduced and developed, and the connections that are drawn
between them.

627D559EFAE44D6491A76CDF60DD9007.description:
Determine a central idea of a text and analyze its development over the course of the text, including
how it emerges and is shaped and refined by specific details; provide an objective summary of the text.

4E7F435EEA7A457687DEF9CC8372BEA6.description:
Cite strong and thorough textual evidence to support analysis of what the text says explicitly as well as
inferences drawn from the text.

3A20CA7E23B6460F9F003ED9F3B5826A.description:
By the end of grade 9, read and comprehend literature, including stories, dramas, and poems, in the
grades 9-10 text complexity band proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range.
By the end of grade 10, read and comprehend literature, including stories, dramas, and poems, at the
high end of the grades 9-10 text complexity band proficiently.

9DBF1E885EC740A18456D26B004F2F34.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

85A71DECF19E414593CA55067E17CFBF.description: Analyze how an author draws on and transforms source material in a specific work.

9C334EAE1F63446F850E397EF73EDABF.description:
Analyze the representation of a subject or a key scene in two different artistic mediums, including what
is emphasized or absent in each treatment.

C46BB40F7CCC42AC8D72FB3BCB5D77E1.description:
Analyze a particular point of view, perspective, or cultural experience reflected in a work of literature
from outside the United States, drawing on a wide reading of world literature.

C39396FA1BBE452AB470B7FE7ECF8576.description:
Analyze how an author’s choices concerning how to structure a text, order events within it (e.g., parallel
plots), and manipulate time (e.g., pacing, flashbacks) create such effects as mystery, tension, or
surprise.

EA9E3444E5E24C3D97EC53752F4DE545.description:
Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in the text, including figurative and
connotative meanings; analyze the cumulative impact of specific word choices on meaning and tone
(e.g., how the language evokes a sense of time and place; how it sets a formal or informal tone).

90420886D2F74C0C87A1A9D9F5D8CB5C.description:
Analyze how complex characters (e.g., those with multiple or conflicting motivations) develop over the
course of a text, interact with other characters, and advance the plot or develop the theme.

8A3AE211E9A947AEB849A85216611D66.description:
Determine a theme or central idea of a text and analyze in detail its development over the course of the
text, including how it emerges and is shaped and refined by specific details; provide an objective
summary of the text.

B8C4DCEE9BD149609CC57201DEE9C386.description:
Cite strong and thorough textual evidence to support analysis of what the text says explicitly as well as
inferences drawn from the text.

standardSets.title: English Language Arts: Grades 11-12
standardSets.subject: English Language Arts and Literacy in History/Social Studies, Science, and Technical Subjects (2024-)

document.title: Iowa Academic Standards for English Language Arts and Literacy in History/Social Studies, Science, and Technical Subjects

5F66C8EEC8BB4342878378A2F0CD62A5.description:
Acquire and use accurately general academic and domain-specific words and phrases, sufficient for
reading, writing, speaking, and listening at the college and career readiness level; demonstrate
independence in gathering vocabulary knowledge when considering a word or phrase important to
comprehension or expression.

BDDCDEFFEDA64E0EA8E5301D9D31E81A.description: Analyze nuances in the meaning of words with similar denotations.

9F04BB5C174E421F9F803EB457A927B1.description:
Interpret figures of speech (e.g., hyperbole, idiom, paradox) in context and analyze their role in
the text.

5B42ED724D15421AB4A15E7F20A44E67.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

324EF9A8EAF74B7181D4D1EFE9D48829.description:
Verify the preliminary determination of the meaning of a word or phrase (e.g., by checking the
inferred meaning in context or by using other reference materials).

D548E936D6DB4529B03402768EC7FE8E.description:
Consult general and specialized reference materials (e.g., dictionaries, glossaries, thesauruses)
to find the pronunciation of a word or determine or clarify its precise meaning, its part of speech,
its etymology, or its standard usage.

30A533B32BE749FBB27AD3E01EABF873.description:
Identify and correctly use patterns of word changes that indicate different meanings or parts of
speech (e.g., conceive, conception, conceivable).

1E6BEAD3E8FD4718875E5A07F6704A27.description:
Use context (e.g., the overall meaning of a sentence, paragraph, or text; a word’s position or
function in a sentence) as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.

370562B773794AEFA77EB42CE7526942.description:
Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on
grades 11–12 reading and content, choosing flexibly from a range of strategies.

2AFA047DF24B43249FEC12F29169B18D.description:
Vary syntax for effect, consulting academic references (e.g., Tufte’s Artful Sentences) for
guidance as needed; apply an understanding of syntax to the study of complex texts when
reading.

7EF06DCACEF5458BAC6549DEFF6A7239.description:
Apply knowledge of language to understand how language functions in different contexts, to make
effective choices for meaning or style, and to comprehend more fully when reading or listening.

EE4D7B95D8B84995B493C1E1A7E7F9E8.description: Spell correctly, consulting references as needed.

A65AE3178F524E338F8C3168B60E5380.description:
Demonstrate appropriate use of complex punctuation (e.g., hyphens, colons, semicolons,
dashes, parenthesis, brackets, ellipsis) both grammatically and for emphasis.

930986A49F974CBC9FB61B0E7D762BB1.description:
Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling
when writing.

2049A1EBEA4A415DBA7D965EDEDF78F1.description: Resolve issues of complex or contested usage, consulting academic references (e.g., MerriamWebster’s Dictionary of English Usage, Garner’s Modern American Usage) as needed.

38C9454DB1DD4582AFDC9B0CD0B45EE3.description:
Apply the understanding that usage is a matter of convention, can change over time, and is
sometimes contested.

5BE15C0FF58241F4BE5F39A2ABF37D82.description:
Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or
speaking.

7D3E87488BFE4704A51D432FAFC3D57E.description:
Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and tasks, such as conducting interviews, participating in public
performances, or debating an issue from either side, demonstrating a command of formal English when
indicated or appropriate; use appropriate eye contact, adequate volume, and clear pronunciation. (See
grades 11–12 Language standards 1 and 3 for specific expectations)

5BC88F924C114FAEA243864889213923.description:
Make strategic use of digital media (e.g., textual, graphical, audio, visual, and interactive elements) in
presentations to enhance understanding of findings, reasoning, and evidence and to add interest.

F72C6788DA5A44DAA1C76DC2015095C2.description:
Present information, findings, and supporting evidence, conveying a clear and distinct perspective,
such that listeners can follow the line of reasoning, alternative or opposing perspectives are addressed,
and the organization, development, substance, and style are appropriate to purpose, audience, and a
range of formal and informal tasks.

740F7F5E27F54719B0257E287E9D4577.description:
Evaluate a speaker’s point of view (perspective), reasoning, and use of evidence and rhetoric,
assessing the stance, premises, links among ideas, word choice, points of emphasis, and tone used.

6782C78BACCF4AEC9D70E369B2881D42.description:
Integrate multiple sources of information presented in diverse formats and media (e.g., visually,
quantitatively, orally) in order to make informed decisions and solve problems, evaluating the credibility
and accuracy of each source and noting any discrepancies among the data.

2F1A5E5DF2B745C7B680FCAFD5896381.description:
Respond thoughtfully to diverse perspectives; synthesize comments, claims, and evidence
made on all sides of an issue; resolve contradictions when possible; and determine what
additional information or research is required to deepen the investigation or complete the task.

19EC487AB598427689D2CC090A044F0A.description:
Propel conversations by posing and responding to questions that probe reasoning and
evidence; ensure a hearing for a full range of positions on a topic or issue; clarify, verify, or
challenge ideas and conclusions; and promote divergent and creative perspectives.

AD770840CD274BBE923BC4F54F082A97.description:
Work with peers to promote civil, democratic discussions and decision-making, set clear goals
and deadlines, and establish individual roles as needed.

958D7A9D7E2543508CA053872DD2A528.description:
Come to discussions prepared, having read and researched material under study; explicitly
draw on that preparation by referring to evidence from texts and other research on the topic or
issue to stimulate a thoughtful, well-reasoned exchange of ideas.

E9D07A477F02455D880E4F051A6CC9B2.description:
Initiate and participate effectively in a range of collaborative discussions (one-on-one, in groups, and
teacher-led) with diverse partners on grades 11–12 topics, texts, and issues, building on others’ ideas
and expressing their own clearly and persuasively.

34450EB8E9BF418D844026F6CC29CC27.description:
Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time
frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of tasks, purposes, and audiences.

5124DED6F38B47CCAF7477A3E3EDCEC3.description:
Apply grades 11–12 Reading standards to literary nonfiction (e.g., “Delineate and evaluate the
reasoning in seminal U.S. texts, including the application of constitutional principles and use of
legal reasoning and the premises, purposes, and arguments in works of public advocacy”).

19DF19FDBEDC4B2EAC344F719E21A1A6.description:
Apply grades 11–12 Reading standards to literature (e.g., “Demonstrate knowledge of
eighteenth-, nineteenth-, twentieth-, and twenty-first-century foundational works of American
literature, including how two or more texts from the same period treat similar themes or topics”).

1159F41E583B4051A4A9725DA82A696D.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

404C60AE47BE42EC91131E3F6FB7FB7F.description:
Gather relevant information from multiple credible primary and secondary authoritative print and digital
sources, using advanced searches effectively; assess the strengths and limitations of each source in
terms of the task, purpose, and audience; integrate information into the text selectively to maintain the
flow of ideas, avoiding plagiarism and overreliance on any one source and following a standard format
for citation.

D5ACB932A4B44FDBA5339144F33D2C13.description:
Conduct short as well as more sustained research projects to answer a question (including a selfgenerated question) or solve a problem; narrow or broaden the inquiry when appropriate; synthesize
multiple sources on the subject, demonstrating understanding of the subject under investigation. (W.11-
12.7)

F8F04F410D2A430DB7AD412A6DCC56FA.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

7BAD1C8199ED4BE6AD4557B1ABFC767B.description:
Use technology to produce, publish, and update individual or shared writing products in response to
ongoing feedback, including new arguments or information.

2603A78B27FA445286C6209BA41174D1.description:
Develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new
approach, focusing on addressing what is most significant for a specific purpose and audience. (Editing
for conventions should demonstrate command of Language standards 1–3 up to and including grades
11–12.)

EA3E9B08392C41CFA158A456717E2407.description:
Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to
task, purpose, and audience. (Grade-specific expectations for writing types are defined in standards 1–
3 above.)

A4A4B5EDFB5D46CE85748B718C8031E1.description:
Provide a conclusion that follows from and reflects on what is experienced, observed, or
resolved over the course of the narrative.

4D7B0C504A1A43E7BCF7B960FAFAB918.description:
Use precise words and phrases, telling details, and sensory language to convey a vivid picture
of the experiences, events, setting, and/or characters.

3B3622DFFB6948D0B87939B8DD48312C.description:
Use a variety of techniques to sequence events so that they build on one another to create a
coherent whole and build toward a particular tone and outcome (e.g., a sense of mystery,
suspense, or resolution).

79D6799858144273B929AB128FA3430C.description:
Use narrative techniques, including dialogue, pacing, description, reflection, and multiple plot
lines, to develop experiences, events, and/or characters; create a smooth progression of
experiences or events.

D0F6F9A1E07C4DDA8041A54A78CB482E.description:
Engage and orient the reader by setting out a problem, situation, or observation and its
significance, establishing one or multiple point(s) of view, and introducing a narrator and/or
characters.

321B9A22213342349520E9412D0C3126.description: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, wellchosen details, and well-structured event sequences.

90ABCC0366F14897B5AD518E73763F26.description:
Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the information or
explanation presented (e.g., articulating implications or the significance of the topic).

7D7EF9A461194402B231CDD7C3E04063.description:
Establish and maintain a formal style and objective tone while attending to the norms and
conventions of the discipline in which they are writing.

7C75A74145E9443FBD4A5CC40377DF93.description:
Use precise language, domain-specific vocabulary, and techniques such as figures of speech
(e.g., metaphor, simile, analogy) or text structure, to manage the complexity of the topic.

F3DD300564894CAAB8D017819193F312.description:
Use appropriate and varied transitions and syntax to link the major sections of the text, create
cohesion, and clarify the relationships among complex ideas and concepts.

7504D4E0B4DA4C9291E6228A1EC7DDA6.description:
Develop the topic clearly and thoroughly by selecting the most significant and relevant facts,
extended definitions, concrete details, quotations, or other information and examples
appropriate to the audience’s knowledge of the topic.

8A16572F1F474813864BDEE5C049DCD2.description:
Introduce a topic; organize complex ideas, concepts, and information so that each new element
builds on that which precedes it to create a unified whole; include formatting (e.g., headings),
graphics (e.g., figures, tables), and multimedia when useful to aiding comprehension.

F2A829BEBD8F4A9A9F8C5DB992323ADD.description:
Write informative/explanatory texts to examine and convey complex ideas, concepts, and information
clearly and accurately through the effective selection, organization, and analysis of content.

9D7630DCC3044F3FABBB889CEFDC30CA.description:
Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the argument
presented, summarizing key points of the argument.

21B153D16E064273AAF83624ED5BAB20.description:
Establish and maintain a formal style and objective tone while attending to the norms and
conventions of the discipline in which they are writing.

DB188ABFBF594F43B89313E613015EDD.description:
Use words, phrases, and clauses as well as varied syntax to link the major sections of the text,
create cohesion, and clarify the relationships between claim(s) and reasons, between reasons
and evidence, and between claim(s) and counterclaims.

426A04C3361A468ABAD9CDED9F1AB55D.description:
Develop claim(s) and counterclaims fairly and thoroughly, supplying the most relevant evidence
for each while pointing out the strengths and limitations of both in a manner that anticipates the
audience’s knowledge level, concerns, values, and possible biases.

5C4E3095AED542E89624B4FFC76517AE.description:
Introduce precise, knowledgeable claim(s), establish the significance of the claim(s), distinguish
the claim(s) from alternate or opposing claims, and create an organization that logically
sequences claim(s), counterclaims, reasons, and evidence.

6C39E470F7434B9CACB73724D14CF426.description:
Write arguments to support claims in an analysis of substantive topics or texts, using valid reasoning
and relevant and sufficient evidence.

EADEE924FC8F4E72BDEDCB7968A216BD.description:
By the end of grade 11, read and comprehend literary nonfiction in the grades 11–CCR text complexity
band proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range.
By the end of grade 12, read and comprehend literary nonfiction at the high end of the grades 11–CCR
text complexity band independently and proficiently.

EA6D21BF870B4851A5270650D667BE09.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

D78B4FD112E44C53A4C24A95ECF26367.description:
Analyze seventeenth-, eighteenth-, nineteenth-, and twentieth-century foundational U.S. documents of
historical and literary significance for their themes, purposes, and rhetorical features.

927499437ED34DFEB59786A5E68FDD19.description:
Delineate and evaluate the reasoning in seminal U.S. texts, including the application of constitutional
principles and use of legal reasoning and the premises, purposes, and arguments in works of public
advocacy.

70DF0ADB8BF04F108E838D579FB976B3.description:
Integrate and evaluate multiple sources of information presented in different media or formats (e.g.,
visually, quantitatively), as well as in words in order to address a question or solve a problem.

A370F843CB334084A94F768E388DF695.description:
Determine an author’s point of view or purpose in a text in which the rhetoric is particularly effective,
analyzing how style and content contribute to the power, persuasiveness, or artistry of the text.

691EDF8E6FD54BE9A52BF00C96A3AE89.description:
Analyze and evaluate the effectiveness of the structure an author uses in their exposition or argument,
including whether the structure makes points clear, convincing, and engaging.

1BA3929C0DF44B08B908C8B86F2C51BD.description:
Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including figurative,
connotative, and technical meanings; analyze how an author uses and refines the meaning of a key
term or terms over the course of a text.

74357C37EB4A4AFF8BF9B72655540E10.description:
Analyze a complex set of ideas or complex sequence of events and explain how specific individuals,
ideas, or events interact and develop over the course of the text.

71C46B3FA1004B5C81C555A7BD0F86D6.description:
Determine two or more central ideas of a text and analyze their development over the course of the
text, including how they interact and build on one another to provide a complex analysis; provide an
objective summary of the text.

3529B9719C004A9DAD4D17971195335C.description:
Analyze and cite strong and thorough textual evidence to support analysis of what the text says
explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the text, including determining where the text leaves room
for subjective interpretation and perspective.

1960C96EBBD54B829B7C3BA97F97CDBA.description:
By the end of grade 11, read and comprehend literature, including stories, dramas, and poems, in the
grades 11-CCR text complexity band proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the
range.
By the end of grade 12, read and comprehend literature, including stories, dramas, and poems, at the
high end of the grades 11-CCR text complexity band independently and proficiently.

16C4A43465284970AE9AD2D504FB17F0.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

BAC3E6F5598541D3869E616FD2BA9ED8.description:
Demonstrate knowledge of eighteenth-, nineteenth-, twentieth-, and twenty-first-century foundational
works of American literature, including how two or more texts from the same period treat similar themes
or topics.

0DFBA1D9F2A84C3DBB8F30E285B8F7A4.description:
Analyze multiple interpretations of a story, drama, or poem (e.g., recorded or live production of a play or
recorded novel or poetry), evaluating how each version interprets the source text. (See list of possible
texts in appendix.)

A2A955BE21BE492198917EC0F4F9A518.description:
Analyze a case in which grasping point of view or perspective requires distinguishing what is directly
stated in a text from what is really meant (e.g., satire, sarcasm, irony, or understatement).

99E576EEAB8A4539954F28B84CE53D69.description:
Analyze how an author’s choices concerning how to structure specific parts of a text (e.g., the choice of
where to begin or end a story, the choice to provide a comedic or tragic resolution) contribute to its
overall structure and meaning as well as its aesthetic impact.

85647CE928E14DE79EFCC3C2FAB49C58.description:
Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in the text, including figurative and
connotative meanings; analyze the impact of specific word choices on meaning and tone, including words with multiple meanings or language that is particularly fresh, engaging, or beautiful.

C52D2048748F48C98ECC6B6807EB19FA.description:
Analyze the impact of the author’s choices regarding how to develop and relate elements of a story or
drama (e.g., where a story is set, how the action is ordered, how the characters are introduced and
developed).

91273502B4D848A68A29D245100CFC02.description:
Determine two or more themes or central ideas of a text and analyze their development over the course
of the text, including how they interact and build on one another to produce a complex account; provide
an objective summary of the text.

DC05D6CA19834BC4AC5507A9860083D4.description:
Analyze and cite strong, clear, and thorough textual evidence to support what the text says explicitly as
well as inferences drawn from the text, including where the text leaves room for subjective
interpretation and perspective.

BAFEB3C3516342D9A2BAA91B8DE8B624.description:

as well as the relevance and sufficiency of the evidence.

and formats, including visually and quantitatively, as well as
in words.*

and style of a text.

10320F4623654F409FC8CE541E79BDB7.description:
Analyze the structure of texts, including how specific
sentences, paragraphs, and larger portions of the text (e.g.,
a section, chapter, scene, or stanza) relate to each other
and the whole.

40899941E2E641CAB4CD4835CEFB269C.description:
Interpret words and phrases as they are used in a text,
including determining technical, connotative, and figurative
meanings, and analyze how specific word choices shape
meaning or tone.

74F39EBC83734CD181C8DA905B917493.description:
Analyze how and why individuals, events, and ideas
develop and interact over the course of a text.

A74312F2F55B4241B4263F77B0451A1B.description:
Determine central ideas or themes of a text and analyze
their development; summarize the key supporting details
and ideas.

E4B2AC7A251B4C95AA69E272E49C7038.description:
Read closely to determine what the text says explicitly and
to make logical inferences from it; cite specific textual
evidence when writing or speaking to support conclusions
drawn from the text.

standardSets.subject: English Language Arts and Literacy in History/Social Studies, Science, and Technical Subjects (2024-)

FEF0692EA8D44314B93636CF29EBF28C.description:
By the end of grade 8, read and comprehend history/social studies texts in the grades 6–8 text
